# The graph

536 concepts from Heidi Priebe's attachment work, linked by typed
relationships. Every claim carries the video and timestamp it came from.

Relationship types: triggers, deactivates, manifests_as (how the pattern runs) ·
defends_against, sustains, originates_in, characterizes (how it is built) ·
healed_by, regulates, requires (what changes it) · mirrors, contrasts_with,
mistaken_for, part_of (how things relate) · described_in, derived_from (sources).

`mirrors` is the most useful one when helping someone: it pairs a move in one
style with its counterpart in another.


## behavior

### Analysing Instead Of Attuning
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's own example, and an unusually candid one: an entire earlier career built on personality models, so that everyone she met could be placed on the right axes. It felt like attunement because she was attuned — to the image of the person assembled in her head. In the room she was half present, measuring what was said against the models. For someone else the frame might be good person or bad, competent or not; the effect is the same.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=700)
  - contrasts_with → Presence And Curiosity Versus Strategy And Analysis (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=740)
  - mirrors → Using The Framework As An Excuse (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=760)
  - source: Attunement: How Securely Attached People Develop Intimacy @700s — https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=700

### Asking Whether They Like You Instead Of Whether You Like Them
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Through the dating phase the running questions are whether you are acceptable to them yet, and how to get them to commit. What goes unasked is whether you like this person, whether they fit your life, whether your futures point the same way. Priebe's point is that the omission does not stay hidden — it surfaces later, as the conflict phase, once the securing is done.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=640)
  - mirrors → Fixating On Whether They Like You (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=620)
  - contrasts_with → Owning Who You Pursue (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=700)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @640s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=640

### Auditing The Timeline
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Stopping on the gaps and contradictions in a partner's account. From inside, this is the avoidant route to changing a feeling — reconstruct what caused it and the state becomes manageable. From the anxious side it lands as a verdict that the feeling is unearned, which is the moment the conversation stops being about the original hurt.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=310)
  - mistaken_for → Minimizing What You Are Going Through (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=380)
  - contrasts_with → Acknowledging The Feeling, Not The Logic (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=400)
  - source: Why Does The Anxious Attachment Style Exaggerate? @310s — https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=310

### Best Behaviour To Get Back In
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Agreeing, at the door, to the amount of space that broke you last time — and knowing in your gut that in six months it will not hold. Priebe says we always know when we are doing this, and names it as a boundary violation in its own right rather than optimism: the other person is being enrolled in a plan on terms you have privately not accepted.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=660)
  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=700)
  - contrasts_with → Agreeing Expectations Explicitly (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=780)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 5 Questions To Ask Yourself Before Getting Back Together With An Ex @660s — https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=660

### Breaking It Off
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Leaving, which does work: at distance the threat cue is gone and the nervous system finally settles.

  - triggers → Longing At A Safe Distance (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=502)

### Burying The Episode
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Filing an incident somewhere you have agreed with yourself never to look. Priebe describes doing this for years with something that turned out, once examined, to need only an apology — the guilt underneath had been unreachable because shame arrived first every time the memory surfaced.

  - contrasts_with → Checking Whether It Pulls You In Or Out (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=660)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=690)
  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @660s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=660

### Confiding In Friends Not The Partner
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The most legible symptom she offers: the people around you knowing more about your frustrations, doubts and private verdicts on your partner than your partner does. In a relationship running in good faith, the partner is the best-informed person about how you feel toward them.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443)
  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @1443s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443

### Decoding An Indirect Partner
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Working out what someone means rather than asking them — a skill built early in a home where people were not direct, and then kept in use by choosing partners who are not either. She notes the tell: the friends get consulted about what the partner is thinking, and the partner does not.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647)
  - mistaken_for → Attunement (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647)
  - source: 10 Signs You May Have An Anxious Attachment Style @647s — https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=647

### Defensiveness
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

What fight-or-flight looks like inside a conversation. She is even-handed that this is not style-specific — everyone does it under threat, and attachment style only decides its shape.

  - source: Cultivating The Ability To Tolerate Emotional Discomfort @70s — https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=70

### Dictating The Solution
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Coming to the conversation with the answer already decided. It can be a good answer and still fail, either because it is not workable for the other person or because they will carry it out while resentment accumulates underneath.

  - triggers → Fear Of Engulfment (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=626)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=626)
  - part_of → Compliance Without Agreement (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=626)
  - source: Navigating Conflict With An Avoidant Partner @626s — https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=626

### Emotional Withdrawal
*behavior · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The visible end of deactivation: less contact, less disclosure, less of oneself brought into the room. Usually read by the other person as a verdict, when it is closer to a reflex.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=2)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @2s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=2
  - triggers → Longing At A Safe Distance (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=502)

### Escalating Anger
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The fight side of the same strategy: making the failure impossible to ignore. She notes it can present as cool and controlled rather than loud — an adult version of a toddler's protest, aimed at the same result.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - contrasts_with → Escalating Vulnerability (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=551)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @430s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430

### Escalating Vulnerability
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

One of the two channels she describes, the fawn side: showing the other person how much you need them so that caring for you becomes the obvious thing to do. In adults it grows more sophisticated but keeps the same shape.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=551)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @430s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430

### Exonerating The Caregiver
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Naming something as harm means saying your feelings were caused by someone else, which is precisely the move this system cannot make. So the past gets recalled as untroubled and even serious mistreatment is reframed as having been deserved or useful — which is also why avoidant adults often cannot locate where their attachment style came from.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=961)
  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @961s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=961

### Fixating On The Partner's Flaws
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Once the threat program is running, flaws are what get logged. Her comparison is being chased through a forest: the scenery is still beautiful, but nobody being chased is looking at it.

  - triggers → Loss Of Attraction (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @607s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=607

### Fixating On Whether They Like You
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious tell for the same moderate range, and a genuinely useful diagnostic: a sudden preoccupation with whether someone is annoyed with you usually means distress has risen somewhere in your life, not necessarily in that relationship. Attention has simply been trained to go looking for closeness whenever the level climbs.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @965s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=965

### Forcing Your Inner State To Conform
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant tell for moderate distress: growing frustrated that you cannot perform at the level you have decided is required, and treating your own depletion as a discipline problem. Rest gets measured against an external standard — eight hours, therefore rested — while the body's actual signal is overruled.

  - triggers → Burnout Collapse (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - mirrors → Fixating On Whether They Like You (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @1449s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1449

### Gaslighting Yourself About Anger
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Meeting each small irritation with an internal ruling that it does not warrant a response. Priebe notes the voice is still there for her, and that its favourite argument — this is too small to bring up — is precisely inverted: smallness is what makes a thing tractable.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=280)
  - contrasts_with → Expressing Anger At Two Out Of Ten (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=500)
  - source: How The Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Deals With Anger @280s — https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=280

### Getting Lost In The Story
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Spending the afternoon narrating the sadness rather than having it, which keeps re-summoning the feeling into the body. Her instruction is to check the body before the mind, since the story is usually running before anyone notices it started.

  - triggers → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891)
  - source: Learning Self-Regulation Through Self-Attunement @891s — https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=891

### Honest Expression Of Need
*behavior · synthesis · secure=secure-form*

Saying what you need plainly, which requires first being in contact with it and able to name it. It is what escalation is a substitute for, and it only becomes possible once needs can be consistently met rather than intermittently extracted.

  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @1326s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1326
  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1326)

### Ignoring People As A Boundary
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

She closes on this: avoidant people often believe boundaries are their strength, when what they are doing is disengaging without ever stating a limit. Withdrawal and a boundary can look identical from outside and differ completely in whether the other person was told anything.

  - mistaken_for → Boundary (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=655)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=655)
  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Boundaries vs Expectations @655s — https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=655

### Insisting You Were Right
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Giving bad directions and then maintaining they were good, with the other person's navigation offered as the explanation. The cost is not the original error — it is that the person's own instrument stops being trustworthy to them.

  - triggers → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - source: Early Experiences Of The Secure Attachment Style @962s — https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962

### Introducing Old Grievances
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Older incidents arriving mid-conflict as further evidence. She reads most of them as stand-ins for the present feeling rather than the real subject — and notes that agreeing to a specific time to discuss one often settles it, because what was needed was the knowledge that you would.

  - triggers → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044)
  - part_of → False Attribution (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044)
  - source: Navigating Conflict With An Anxiously Attached Partner @1044s — https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=1044

### Letting A Relationship Go
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary · sign of change*

A sign of change rather than a loss: recognising a relationship where what you need is not on offer, and stopping — without the frantic push to get the person to see it differently. She frames the inner work as only half of it; the other half is making your surroundings match.

  - contrasts_with → Pursuing Inconsistent Partners (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123)
  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123)
  - source: 5 Struggles Securely Attached People Still Have @123s — https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=123

### Letting The Pain Land
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: registering the cost of an interaction while it is happening rather than reconstructing it later without the charge. Her point is that this is where boundaries come from — pain is the instrument that tells you what to avoid, and without it you can only conclude that everything is survivable.

  - contrasts_with → Pain Hidden From Yourself (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=966)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @966s — https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=966

### Looking Down On The Partner
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Contempt made operational. Writing the other person off as incapable removes the need to be vulnerable with them — and removes their chance to do better, because they are no longer being handed anything real to meet.

  - triggers → The Partner's Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @1092s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092

### Loving Too Hard
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her sharpest reframe in this video, and an uncomfortable one. Persisting with someone who has said what they want, when it is not you, is not an excess of generosity — it is declining to take their answer. Giving to someone not asking to receive looks like devotion from inside and like a boundary being crossed from outside.

  - mistaken_for → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @122s — https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=122

### Making It A Relationship Issue
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Rather than saying this matters to me, saying that it is important for a relationship — which is harder to refuse and cannot be rejected personally. Priebe's objection is what it costs: dressing a want as a principle also removes the chance of the want itself being seen and taken seriously.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=520)
  - contrasts_with → Honest Expression Of Need (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=540)
  - mistaken_for → Framing It As A Shared Problem (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=530)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @520s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=520

### Manufacturing A Reason For The Feeling
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

If raw feeling will not be taken seriously, the anxious partner supplies a rationale that will. Priebe's example: irritation at a partner newly working from home, unexplained, gets recast as worry about money and the mortgage — and now the couple is having a detailed conversation on a level where the problem does not exist. The real one was needing time alone.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=850)
  - mirrors → Exaggerating The Story (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=830)
  - contrasts_with → Bringing The Feeling Without An Explanation (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=950)
  - source: Top 10 Mistakes Anxious/Avoidant Couples Make (And How To Fix Them) @850s — https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=850

### Minimizing What You Are Going Through
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Reflexively shrinking the account of what is happening to you, often past the point of plausibility. She notes the social cost is usually misread: people conclude you are unfriendly or uninterested, when what they are seeing is someone managing another person's concern away.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - triggers → Self-Disgust At Your Own Need (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - mistaken_for → Ignoring People As A Boundary (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651)
  - source: Why Does The Avoidant Attachment Style Fear Intimacy? @651s — https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=651

### Mistaking Attraction For A Decision
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

For most people attraction is a yellow light — reason to find out more. For the anxious system it settles the question. Priebe notes what does not then happen: the getting-to-know-you that would establish whether this person fits a life, because the enquiry has already moved on to how to be wanted by them.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=500)
  - mistaken_for → Chosen Excitement (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=510)
  - contrasts_with → Reviewing The Relationship Objectively (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=530)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @500s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=500

### Naming The Fantasy
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: spotting the invented version while it is running, and letting the real person be disappointing rather than treating the gap as something they owe you. She puts it plainly — you do not get to be angry at someone for not following a script they were never shown.

  - contrasts_with → Limerence (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=321)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @321s — https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=321

### Partner Stops Rising To The Occasion
*behavior · the partner's side · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The other half of the loop. Handed no real responsibility and no honest account of what hurt, the partner has nothing to respond to competently — which is then read as confirmation that they never could.

  - triggers → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @1092s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092

### Pursuing Inconsistent Partners
*behavior · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Saying, sincerely, that what you want is someone emotionally available, and then not pursuing them when they appear. The responsive partner does not register as the thing being searched for.

  - characterizes → Anxious-Preoccupied (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @430s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=430

### Putting People On Pedestals
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her example is imagining a rich inner life in a reserved partner and growing frustrated when it does not surface. The corrective she offers is a sorting question worth asking often: what did this person actually tell me or show me, and what did I supply on their behalf?

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970)
  - part_of → Negative View Of Self, Positive View Of Others (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970)
  - source: 10 Signs You May Have An Anxious Attachment Style @970s — https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970

### Putting Your Own Needs Aside
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Setting down what you need in order to attend to someone else's difficulty. Done once it is generosity; done as a standing position it accrues a debt the other person never agreed to.

  - triggers → Resentment (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374)
  - source: Attachment Styles & The Drama Triangle (Part 1): Intro To The Drama Triangle @374s — https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=374

### Recognizing Your Own Vulnerability
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating · sign of change*

A sign of change: locating the places, past or present, where you needed care and did not get it — without first requiring a justification for why it counts. She describes it as recognising impact regardless of circumstance.

  - contrasts_with → Everything That Happens Is My Doing (https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=256)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @256s — https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=256

### Refining The Ideal Partner
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The failure loop she describes: leave a bad relationship, get more specific about the traits to avoid, and find each successive partnership contains less of the bad without ever becoming the good one. The work feels like progress and is really goalpost movement, because the search is still for someone who will do the protecting.

  - triggers → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607)
  - part_of → The Deflated Wheel (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607)
  - mistaken_for → Reading Your Relationship History (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @607s — https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=607

### Returning To The Relationship
*behavior · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The return, which restores the closeness — and with it the conditions that started the sequence.

*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Needing every conversation to reach the core immediately, and finding anything lighter unbearable. Her analogy is compulsive eating: someone who eats without attention is not savouring food, whatever their enthusiasm for it — and the same distinction separates savouring closeness from consuming it.

### Scanning For Confirmation
*behavior · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Searching the partner for any small indication that the feared thing is true — and finding one, because a search that specific always does. What was a fear then arrives back as confirmed knowledge.

### Self-Punishment Instead Of Amends
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Going through enough private misery about something that it starts to feel settled. Priebe's correction is blunt: the harm done to the other person does not decrease by any amount of self-hatred. Shame is so consuming that it crowds out the other person's perspective entirely, which is exactly the perspective repair requires.

### Stating A Surface Grievance
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The complaint offered in conflict, which is sincerely meant and is not the operative one. Her paired examples: the avoidant partner wanting to avoid drama, where what is being avoided is the exposure of saying what they need; the anxious partner wanting things to be alright, where what is urgent is the return of co-regulation.

### Suppressing The Other Side
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Entering the next relationship determined to keep the unwanted half out of sight. It works for a while, which is the problem — the partner meets it later and with less warning, so it lands harder. She describes the result as an escalating cycle: each attempt to hide it better produces more chaos when the lid finally comes off.

Declining to state a want at the point where stating it feels most dangerous. Sometimes the need is actively disclaimed out loud, which is what makes it land as a change of terms rather than a disclosure when it surfaces later.

Producing a vivid account designed to induce an emotional reaction rather than saying the emotion outright. Priebe reads this as the safer of two moves: the story can be argued with, but naming the feeling and the need directly exposes them, so the story goes first.

Other people's visible need stops registering as an offence. She is precise that this does not require agreeing with them — you may still think a display is overdone — only that it no longer lands at the level of anger, because the rule it was breaking has loosened in you.

The other misuse, and the mirror of the first: taking the diagnosis as a licence rather than a starting point. ### Using The Framework To Manipulate
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The misuse she calls the largest online: learning someone's style in order to route around what they have said they want. Her argument is that the move is self-defeating on its own terms — attempting to override another person's stated wishes is itself an insecure response, and security is precisely the capacity to take someone at face value. She notes recovery programmes carry an explicit rule against using their own language this way, for the same reason.

  - mistaken_for → Taking Your Partner At Face Value (https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=241)

### Venting Instead Of Being Vulnerable
*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe separates seeking support from building a case. Describing your partner as terrible so a friend will say leave them is not the vulnerable version; the vulnerable version is saying you do not know how to fix it, that you are in pain, that you are afraid of being told to leave, and that you are not ready to. The first keeps the shame intact; only the second gets you anything.

  - mistaken_for → Confiding In Friends Not The Partner (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1210)
  - contrasts_with → Comfort From Someone Other Than The One Who Hurt You (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1230)

*behavior · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core · sign of change*

A sign of change rather than a symptom: noticing that the system is pulling in several directions at once, and treating that as a reason not to act rather than a reason to act urgently.

*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The assumption Priebe says attachment work rarely challenges: that you get healthier and your existing life improves around you. Her counter is that a life has usually been built out of situations the old strategy navigates well, and some of them — including sources of livelihood and of genuine connection — will not survive the change.

  - healed_by → Mapping Where The Strategy Works (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=1000)
  - contrasts_with → Changing The Environment, Not Just The Response (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=890)

### I Can Only Feel Better Through Someone Else
*belief · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The blind spot left by learning co-regulation without self-regulation. A strong feeling is understood to be something that ends when another person makes it end, so being alone with one reads as being stuck with it permanently.

### I Can Protect Myself But Not Comfort Myself
*belief · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant inverse. Behaving correctly heads off rejection, so protection is learnable — but if pain lands anyway you are alone with it. She notes this rarely presents as refusing help: reaching out simply never occurs to the person as an option.

### I Cannot Be Okay Until They Change
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her single test for whether you are in the triangle. The grievance may be entirely legitimate — someone may genuinely have wronged you — and it makes no difference: while your wellbeing waits on somebody else's move, it is not in your hands. She names this as the thing that has to go before attachment work can begin at all.

### I Cannot Protect Myself, Only Be Comforted
*belief · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

What follows from receiving comfort without protection. Distress becomes something that happens to you and is then relieved by someone else, rather than something you could have headed off — so the useful skill is keeping people close, not preventing the spike.

### I Intend To Die With These Parts Unseen
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Not a decision to be private but a standing plan that the shameful parts stay hidden permanently. Priebe contrasts it with the secure pattern, which also does not disclose everything immediately but does disclose progressively as trust accumulates. The plan is what makes intimacy something that can only happen by accident.

### I Lost Myself In That Relationship
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The central error she names, and the one that guarantees repetition. Seeing the suppressed half emerge under pressure, the conclusion drawn is that the partner produced it — so the next search is for someone who will not. Her correction is exact: nothing was lost in that relationship, something was found that is normally kept out of view.

### I Was Not Clear Enough
*belief · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The reading a child makes of intermittent success. If the same signal works sometimes and fails other times, the difference must lie in how clearly it was sent — so the answer is to send it louder. This is the premise underneath every escalation.

### I Will Be Loved If I Am Needed
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The premise underneath rescuing. If care is something you earn by being indispensable, then making yourself indispensable is the strategy — which means quietly needing the other person not to become able to manage.

### I Will Only Be Happy Once You Meet My Needs
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The unconscious sentence running underneath anxious conflict, and the definition of the victim corner. It was learned honestly: press hard enough on what hurts and the caregiver came. Priebe notes the adult version pushes an avoidant partner away precisely because it works by crossing the boundary they are most defended around.

### I Would Contaminate A Healthy Person
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The anxious style doubts its desirability while holding that it is fundamentally well-meaning with a lot of love to give. The avoidant holds that it is solid and has plenty to offer practically. The fearful-avoidant, seeing its own strategic and manipulative moves clearly, concludes that it is bad — and so rejects the person offering healthy love, to protect them from it.

### I Would Not Be Compatible With Someone Healthier
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A belief Priebe declines to simply refute. Stated as worth — nobody better would want me — it is false. Stated as skill — I do not yet have the equipment to relate to someone who communicates well — it is often accurate, and it names the actual work. The two readings feel identical from inside and lead to opposite conclusions.

*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The conclusion a scapegoated child reaches, carried into adulthood as a standing veto on low-grade anger. ### If It Does Not Make Sense I Am Not Feeling It
*belief · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant bias: when a feeling has no defensible cause, the feeling is judged mistaken and reassigned to something else — too much coffee, not enough exercise. She points out this repeats the misattunement inward, telling yourself the thing happening in your body is not happening.

### If It Doesn't Hurt Me, It Doesn't Hurt Them
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant does not know their pain response is quieter than other people's, so their own reading becomes the reference. A partner in visible distress over something that would barely register is therefore performing, or angling for something. Priebe treats this as the honest source of a great deal of avoidant impatience — a calibration error, not contempt.

### If My Feeling Is Strong, Something Caused It
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Learned early and often accurate: a child in an unpredictable home whose feelings tracked what was going on around them. Carried into adulthood it becomes a rule — an intense feeling must have an external cause — with no room for a state that arose from somewhere else entirely and then went looking for something to attach to.

### If You Felt What I Feel, You Would Help Me
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Under activation the anxious system treats transmitting the feeling as the only route to relief: if the other person could be made to feel what I feel, they would give me the co-regulation that ends it. This makes accuracy about events negotiable — the story is instrumental, the feeling is the message.

*belief · synthesis · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Having formed its model of relationships around unpredictability, the system recognises unpredictability as the thing it is looking for. This is why the stated wish for a responsive partner and the actual pursuit so often point in opposite directions.

### Inside A Relationship I Cannot Have Boundaries
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Never having seen a boundary held inside an intimate relationship as a child, the adult concludes that partnership means total absorption — no asking for space, no asking for anything the other person does not already want. Which leaves exit as the only door to solitude, and makes every need for room look like a reason to leave.

*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fear that keeps the box shut: that admitting the repressed half will mean being ruled by it. Her answer is that the opposite happens — what integration produces is discernment about which side to weight when, where the unintegrated version simply gets overtaken at unpredictable moments.

The surface-level fear, and the reason avoidant people can look uncompromising from outside. It is rarely unwillingness to make room — it is that the scaffolding keeping them steady was built over decades without other people in it, and closeness threatens every piece of it at once.

The fearful-avoidant premise: deep connection with someone who sees only the vulnerabilities you have selected for them. The catch she names is that the material being withheld is the material intimacy is actually built from, so the premise rules out the thing it is asking for.

The avoidant version of an impossible expectation, and the mirror of the anxious one. Where one demands that a relationship dissolve all insecurity, this demands a partner who never needs anything managed — and treats any lapse as evidence of the wrong person rather than of a person.

Strength read as self-sufficiency: needing nothing from anyone, never asking, handling it. Priebe separates appearing capable from being capable — the cost of the appearance is the perspective, feedback and complementary skill that only come from other people, plus the knowledge of what you do not know, which she treats as a component of competence rather than a concession.

### Once I Am Healed I Will Not Be Emotional
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Every style carries a slightly wrong picture of what recovery looks like, and this is the fearful-avoidant one: the emotions and needs that break through are read as the malfunction, so healing means stopping them. Priebe's counter runs the other way — the route out is making attachment needs more conscious day to day, not less, which is precisely what feels wrong.

*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe grants this one a great deal of ground. Fearful-avoidant lives often do not follow the ordinary sequence, and the coping machinery built around a complex history is genuinely hard for others to read — so finding someone who does understand is rare, and letting go of them is correspondingly hard. She calls that reasonable, and then notes what it costs when the rare person is also the wrong one.

The conclusion drawn from repeated refusal. Not a judgement about emotion but a conditioned finding about what works: needs get met by appearing not to have any, or by having only the pleasant ones.

### Something Is Wrong With Me
*belief · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The deepest layer, and she says every insecure style holds some version of it. For avoidant patterning the shame attaches to having needs at all — without the accompanying knowledge that everyone has them and that secure people simply do not carry shame about it. Because a self-rejecting layer sits on top, someone else responding warmly is not enough to shift it.

### The Redemption Fantasy
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The wager underneath limerence: that things become permanently alright if this particular person can be got to care in this particular way. It is why disconfirming evidence tends to raise the effort rather than lower it — the fantasy is doing a job, and losing it costs more than being wrong does.

### The Relationship Will Fix How I Feel
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The romantic form of the same premise: once a committed relationship is in place there will finally be someone permanently available to regulate you. She notes how much of our art and film encodes exactly this, which is part of why it goes so long unexamined.

### Vulnerability In A Partner Is Unattractive
*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The fifth blindspot, and the most zoomed-out: which people you keep choosing. If the pattern is partners who present as sunny and unbothered, with the emotional availability expected to arrive later, it is worth asking whether availability is in fact a turn-off. Secure people show their feelings and expect the secure-base role to alternate — so the preference and the stated goal are pulling in opposite directions.

*belief · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Learned where reaching out was reliably met with withdrawal or hostility. It is held as a bodily prediction rather than an opinion, which is why it keeps operating in people who would sincerely deny believing it.

*belief · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The opposite distortion from the avoidant one, and she puts them side by side: where one person cannot see that anything was done to them, the other cannot see that anything was done by them. Both miss the same middle.

## concept

### A Non-Zero Chance Beats Zero
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The arithmetic that keeps the pattern running. A house with heating ten per cent of the time still beats an outdoors with none, so it is rational to stay inside and work on the boiler. Priebe's point is that the fixation on getting a dysregulated partner regulated again is not irrational attachment — it is the only option with a probability above zero, and the unconscious has done the maths.

  - part_of → The Intimacy Desert (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=450)
  - mirrors → Monitoring The Bond (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=500)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidant: How Intimacy Scarcity Keeps You Codependent (And How To Change It) @450s — https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=450

### A Pervasive Sense Of Self
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Holding an account of who you are that does not require confirmation from the conversation you are currently in. With it, being misunderstood is temporary and survivable; without it, disagreement lands as an identity threat, and what someone else believes about you becomes something you have to win.

  - part_of → Realistic Cause And Effect (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)
  - contrasts_with → I Am Not Okay And Neither Are You (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)

### A Reasonable Need Is Not An Obligation
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious version of fairness runs: if what I want is reasonable, they ought to provide it. Priebe declines the inference. Your need can be entirely reasonable and this person can still be unwilling — and what you hold is not a claim on them but the choice of who you are with. If the pattern repeats across partners, the question moves to how much you are routing through one relationship.

  - part_of → Nobody Is Required To Give You Their Attention (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=760)
  - mirrors → Setting A Boundary You Control (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=790)
  - contrasts_with → I Cannot Be Okay Until They Change (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=800)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 5 Questions To Ask Yourself Before Getting Back Together With An Ex @760s — https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=760

### Accidental Bad Faith
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her central coinage here. In law or debate, arguing in bad faith means knowingly pushing an agenda other than the stated one. In an insecure dynamic the same structure appears without the knowing: the real want is hidden from the person holding it. Functionally it behaves identically — the stated issue never resolves, because neither party is actually arguing about it.

  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @393s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=393
  - part_of → Unconscious Relationship Premise (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=513)

### Accidental Intimacy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant keeps the shame-bound material — which is to say, ordinary human emotion — out of every social and professional setting, and it surfaces only where self-control fails: inside a close relationship, under trigger. So the one experience of being fully known arrives as a by-product of the worst moments, and belongs exclusively to the relationship that produced them.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=140)

### Adaptive Versus Healthy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Something can be exactly right for the situation that produced it and ruinous over a lifetime. Priebe insists the insecure strategy was the correct answer to the home it was formed in — not a defect, not stupidity — and that the only route to a healthier response runs through understanding what environment you were solving for.

### All My Exes Were Narcissists
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe refuses this as an answer to what has gone wrong before — not because it is never true of any individual, but because as an account of a pattern it names the obstacle and then declines to work on it. If the partners keep turning out that way, the thing in the way is what you are drawn to, and that is the item on the list before the next relationship.

### Allergic To The Medicine
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant needs love as much as anyone and reacts badly to it in quantity, so it has to be taken in small amounts and spaced out. That is the shape of the slow approach — a little closeness, then distance to manage the reaction, then a little more — repeated for years. Intimacy is the trigger because intimacy once meant your boundaries were about to go.

  - part_of → The Emotional Immune System (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1100)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1240)

### An Unspoken Boundary Guarantees A Repeat
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Slipping away, going quiet and hoping the other person works it out leaves them with no information, so the next attempt comes with more force — and the situation recurs at higher intensity. Priebe's structure for the avoidant is that the end of the sequence is right (go and regulate alone) and the middle is missing: say what is wrong, what is unacceptable, and what would need to change.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=740)

### Anger Is Self-Correcting
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Stated the first time a line is crossed, anger usually stops the crossing. Stated the tenth time, it arrives alongside nine occasions on which you said nothing — which weakens your own footing, because you were the one who let it stand. The function of anger is corrective, and it only performs that function on time.

  - part_of → The Anger Scale (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=480)

### Asking For Help Feels Natural
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Needs were met early without having to be exaggerated or fought for, so the adult expects the same ordinary reciprocation: I say what I need, you supply it if you can, and if you cannot you say so. The insecure styles find asking hard and receiving harder. Priebe notes the secure person also gives help readily, which is part of why asking feels unremarkable.

### Attunement
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Reading another person's state, letting your own respond to it, and reflecting it back accurately before helping settle it. Her image is a caregiver meeting a crying infant with a face that matches the distress rather than contradicts it — the child sees its inner state confirmed, and only then soothed.

  - contrasts_with → Misattuned Mirroring (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=200)
  - source: Learning Self-Regulation Through Self-Attunement @200s — https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=200

### Attunement Is Not Only The Loud Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's answer to the standard objection — that attending to your feelings would make you irrational and idle. She borrows the intuitive-eating case: the fear is that you would live on pizza, but genuine attunement includes noticing which foods leave you flat and which are easy on you. Emotionally the same holds. The system that says stay in bed is also the system that wants to feel proud of itself and will supply the discipline.

  - mirrors → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=500)
  - contrasts_with → Anything That Feels Bad Is Bad (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=560)

### Avoidance Is A Misnomer
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

To avoid a thing you have to know it is there. Priebe's objection to the label is that the dismissive type is mostly not declining to look — the painful thought does not reach awareness at all. Conscious avoidance of distressing thoughts is more characteristic of the anxious and fearful-avoidant types. Her own names would be closer to oblivious and obsessive, which she concedes would not catch on.

  - part_of → Not A Personality Type (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=250)

### Avoidants Are Not Villains
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Popular attachment writing tends to sympathise with the anxious style and warn people away from the avoidant one. Priebe rejects that split: the avoidant adaptation is as involuntary and as early as the anxious one, and describing it as a character flaw makes it harder for avoidant people to recognise themselves in the material at all.

### Awareness Is Not The Solution
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A correction Priebe returns to across her work and states plainly here: people reaching stage two assume that because they can see the problem they should be able to solve it, and conclude something is wrong with them when they cannot. Seeing it and being able to do otherwise are separate acquisitions, and the gap between them is the healing process rather than a failure inside it.

### Babies Cannot Be Manipulative
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe stops to rule this out explicitly. An infant lacks the equipment for manipulation; it is running trial and error and keeping whatever works. If expressing the real feeling was punished and expressing a different one was rewarded, the child learns the substitution without ever forming the intention. The same behaviour in an adult, with adult capacities, is another matter.

### Balancing Pain With An Extreme High
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant feels pain at anxious volume and co-regulates like an avoidant — which is to say, barely. Unable to sit with it and unwilling to be vulnerable about it, they offset it with something large: the sudden travel, the enormous ambition, the extravagant redirection. Priebe notes all insecure styles cope badly at times; what is specific here is having the anxious level of pain with the avoidant level of support.

### Base Strategy With Trauma Intrusions
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

One account of fearful-avoidant development that Priebe finds useful: a single base strategy — say, avoidant — with trauma triggers that periodically flip the system into its opposite. Downplay everything most of the time; then a flashback arrives and the response overshoots into amplification or aggression. Run often enough, it stops looking like intrusions and starts looking like a style.

### Becoming Worthy Of Someone Self-Sufficient
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious appraisal of a new person is an audit of what they have that you lack — charm, confidence, ease — and a private conclusion that you will never have it, but could acquire it by being loved by someone who does. Hence the paradox: real investment in self-improvement, aimed not at becoming self-sufficient but at becoming the sort of person a self-sufficient person would choose.

### Being Accurately Decoded
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her metaphor for what an infant is actually up against: waking on an unfamiliar planet with a single guide who controls everything you need, and only emotion to communicate with. A guide fluent in your language is a relief; one who catches a tenth of it is frightening. The two insecure strategies are the two available responses to being misread — send the signal harder, or stop sending and go looking alone.

### Being Idealised Is Comfortable And Costly
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A partner who finds you flawless confirms the I-am-okay-you-are-not model, and is therefore easy to be around — and cannot tolerate it when you eventually bring something real. Meanwhile a secure partner noticing where you are struggling registers as criticism, or as being found insufficient, when it is usually just attention. Priebe's ask is to get comfortable being seen whole, unfinished parts included.

### Being The Same Person Everywhere
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her stated end point for fearful-avoidant healing. The test she offers is concrete: how a partner would describe you should broadly match how friends, family and colleagues would. Her image for the mechanism is oxygen — parts of us kept shut away go strange in the dark and emerge strangely; exposed a little at a time to people who can be trusted with them, they grow into something ordinary.

### Better Is A Relational Skill
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Insecure attachment tends to read self-improvement as raising your score on visible variables — fitness, money, being interesting. Priebe's claim is that those recruit people who also rank on those variables and do not know how to connect. What actually makes healthy love available is the capacity to stay regulated while holding someone else's complexity, including the parts of it that threaten you.

### Blaming The Relationship For What You Stopped Doing
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's own repeated pattern: disciplined about health and work when single, and then, on entering any relationship, unconsciously avoiding all conflict and putting her own needs behind her partner's — until one day she looked across and concluded he was why her career had stalled. The partner had not asked for any of it. The abandonment was hers, and it made the fantasy of leaving look correct.

### Both Feel They Give More
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The anxious partner gives constantly and feels unvalued, because what is given is the thing the other is allergic to. The avoidant partner keeps themselves level through everything life throws and feels unvalued too, because they are also expected to absorb someone else's crises. Priebe's observation is that in these pairings both people believe, accurately from where they stand, that they are carrying it.

  - mirrors → Projecting Your Own Remedy (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1500)

### Boundary
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A decision about what you will do, enforceable no matter what anyone else chooses. Her test is ownership: a boundary is a fence built on your own side of the property line, so nobody else can take it down. If keeping it requires someone else to behave a particular way, it is not one.

  - contrasts_with → Expectation (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=90)
  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Boundaries vs Expectations @2s — https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=2

### Changing The Environment, Not Just The Response
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Half of the work is behaving securely in the situations you are already in. The other half is noticing which situations you selected because the old strategy handles them, and moving. Priebe's line is that you cannot get healthy while unprotected in a sick environment — trying to be secure where insecure responses are genuinely the most adaptive is not a fair test of anything.

  - part_of → Where The Strategy Still Works (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=700)

### Chosen Excitement
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her answer to the worry that security is flat. The intensity of insecure attachment is largely reactive — you are responding to whatever temporarily makes you feel alright. With a stable baseline, the adventure is selected rather than arriving at you, and she rates the two as not really comparable.

### Closeness Is Not Sameness
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's improv story makes the point better than the theory does. A friendship had gone flat while she deferred to what the other person wanted; in a class exercise where each character held a private objective, the interplay came straight back. Wanting something that had nothing to do with his approval was what put energy between them. Intimacy needs edges — otherwise nobody can tell where one of you stops.

### Co-Regulation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Two nervous systems settling each other. Mostly mundane — getting used to someone replying, to their presence in a week — rather than the dramatic comforting the word suggests, which is why becoming dependent on it goes unnoticed.

### Co-Regulation Toward Independence
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her sharpest distinction in this video: much of what passes for co-regulation in insecure relationships is the drama triangle with one partner rescuing. The secure version leaves both people more able to manage, not less — closeness offered as a reminder of what you can do, rather than as the thing standing in for it.

### Comfort From Someone Other Than The One Who Hurt You
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The wound underneath fearful-avoidance is having needed comfort from the person causing the distress, with no alternative available. The belief that follows is that only the source of the pain can relieve it. Priebe treats breaking that specific link — learning to seek real support outside the relationship the trouble is in — as the single highest-leverage move available to the style.

### Commitment As A Life Sentence Of Self-Erasure
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's reframe of avoidant commitment fear. If being in a relationship means obeying the rulebook, then committing means obeying it for life — and the resistance is accurate. Secure people commit easily not because they are braver but because they are not betraying themselves: when an arrangement stops working they renegotiate it. The fear is of the terms, not of the person.

### Compartmentalising Yourself To Stay
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Entering a relationship having decided in advance which parts of you will not appear, on the grounds that the whole version would not be accepted. Priebe puts it in the harshest terms she uses anywhere: it tells the most vulnerable part of you that it can be traded for someone else's approval, and it works on self-esteem over years the way you would expect.

### Complex Causality
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The security position, and the exit from the blame see-saw: most conflicts are produced by two people acting in good faith whose triggers and unexamined programmes collide. Not because either is malicious, but because communicating across two histories is difficult and needs continuous renegotiation. Priebe calls the alternative — one of you is doing it all wrong — a false dichotomy in both directions.

### Compliance Without Agreement
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A relationship where the instructions get carried out and the resentment quietly builds. She names it as the failure mode of solving a conflict on one person's terms: agreement reached by collaboration is the only kind either party actually wants to keep.

### Conflict Is Uncomfortable, Not Catastrophic
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Secure people generally do not enjoy conflict and are willing to have it, because they either saw it resolved peacefully or learned later that it can be. Priebe's sharpest observation is about what the insecure styles are missing: not the courage but the knowledge — at a gut level they do not know that a direct conversation which simply settles something is an available outcome.

### Conscious Competence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Being able to notice the trigger and do something other than the old thing — with full effort, every time, against what feels like your own grain. Priebe says this stage often takes years and is the one people quit in, and that the feedback loop back into stage two is normal rather than a relapse.

### Conscious Incompetence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Seeing the problem clearly and having none of the equipment to solve it — which Priebe rates the most frustrating stage of the four, because the awareness arrives long before the capacity does. Its actual job is observation: when the triggering happens, what precedes it, which parts of life it reaches. People want to skip it and cannot.

### Consciously Adapting To Each Relationship
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Feeling avoidant around some people and anxious around others is not evidence of fearful-avoidance — most people pull back a little from a surplus of anxious energy and lean in a little toward someone who gives them nothing to read. Secure people do the same thing deliberately: take a little space here, try a bit harder there, without an outer critic and without insult when a text goes unanswered.

### Containment
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

Holding another person's experience in your own mind in a way they cannot yet, running it through an adult's processing, and handing back something they can use. Absorb, mirror accurately, then help them find a response. A child arrives with no template for anger or sadness and learns what to do with it from what comes back.

### Controlling How Your Partner Feels About You
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe notes the gap between the popular picture of anxious attachment — sympathetic, deprived of love — and what the literature actually describes, which is controlling. Not usually overt: the control is over how the partner feels, so that they stay aligned and connected and the co-regulation stays available. She adds that you would be hard pressed to find an anxious person who recognises it, because it runs below the level of choice.

### Deactivation As A Response To Your Own Rules
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's worked example. A long-distance partner was going to visit; within days she was cataloguing everything wrong with them and losing attraction. What had actually happened was a rule switching on — while they are in my space I may not ask for time alone, refuse closeness, or have needs of my own — and the disgust was a response to that sentence, which her partner had never uttered. The rules were hers, and she had assigned them to him.

### Decision Paralysis And The Empty Milestone
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Emotions are what tell you what matters, so losing access to them breaks decision-making at both scales. At the large scale you follow other people's formula for a good life, hit the milestones, and cannot work out why arriving feels like nothing. At the small scale you can spend an hour on dinner or a shirt, because with no guiding principles the only available signal is the next small hit.

### Detaching Is Not A Boundary
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Avoidant people often believe their boundaries are excellent because they are very good at detaching. Priebe separates the two: detaching is a trauma response, and a boundary is being clear about a need, saying what the limit is and why, and then living inside it. Boundaries make interdependence possible; detachment produces counter-dependence, which is a different thing wearing the same word.

### Differentiation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Knowing where you end and another person begins — which feeling in the room is yours. An infant cannot yet tell itself apart from its caregiver, and where that separation is never properly completed, the adult keeps mistaking their own state for someone else's.

### Direction Of Travel
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Each insecure style is moving toward something it never arrives at. The anxious person is going for relationship security and keeps finding another floor below the one they reached. The avoidant person is going for complete self-sufficiency. The fearful-avoidant has no settled direction at all — approach and exit alternate — which is why the pattern is disorienting from the inside as much as from outside.

### Disorganized Attachment
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The infant classification the fearful-avoidant adult style is correlated with. It was named for an absence rather than a presence: where avoidant infants consistently disengage and anxious infants consistently escalate, these infants showed no coherent strategy in either direction — moving toward the caregiver, then freezing or turning away.

### Distorted Emotion And Distorted Logic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The clean statement of the mirror. Under pressure anxious patterning trusts the feeling and arranges reasoning to fit it; avoidant patterning trusts the reasoning and arranges feeling to fit that. Neither is available to the other in the moment, which is why one partner offering to correct the other's logic reads as a refusal to believe them.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant runs both patterns and so has both jobs: find where the pain receptors are muted and sensitize to what is being felt but not registered, and learn to regulate in the areas where the pain is already loud and constant. Priebe adds that the identity confusion — am I the tough one or the needy one — is itself a symptom of running both.

### Doubling Down Under Stress
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Ambiguity and external threat are precisely when co-regulation is worth most, and precisely when both parties revert hardest — the avoidant to control or detachment, the anxious to fixation, each aimed at the other. Priebe's alternative is not agreement but alliance: this situation is hard, our needs differ, neither of us has to be shamed for that, and it helps to have someone to hold on to.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's analogy for the avoidant end: being unable to feel physical pain looks like an advantage and is disabling, because pain is the alerting system — stop, this is damage, rest. Emotional pain does the same job. It flags when the thing you are doing is wrong for you and when someone is treating you badly, and a system that mutes it loses the warning, not just the discomfort.

*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

What Priebe identifies as the real difference between the secure and the anxious childhood: not whether the child was soothed, but whether anyone was seen handling their own distress. Secure children watch a parent go into discomfort and come out of it, and acquire the sequence. Being comforted without ever seeing that leaves you able to be regulated and unable to do it yourself.

### Emotionally Organised Versus Temporally Organised
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's account of why the same argument reads so differently from each side. The anxious system organises reality around felt experience: what is true about this situation is what I am feeling. The avoidant system organises it around sequence: what is true is the order of events that produced the state. Neither is lying. They are indexing reality on different keys, and each reads the other's key as an evasion.

### Emotions As Currency
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her framing for what an infant's emotional display actually is: the only means it has of purchasing care. Crying buys soothing, anger buys an injustice being noticed, fear buys protection. An avoidant childhood is one where that currency was consistently refused at the counter, so the child learned to obtain things by not offering it.

  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @228s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=228

### Empathy Without Being Overwhelmed
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Neither drowning in another person's pain nor keeping away from it in case you would. Priebe attributes it to having been contained as a child — a caregiver who saw the pain, reflected it back and was not themselves capsized by it. She notes that one common use of the word empath describes the anxious version instead: unable to tell what is theirs and what is yours, so it all has to be felt.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=1000)
  - part_of → Containment (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=1020)

  - source: 10 Signs You May Have A Secure Attachment Style @1000s — https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=1000

### Enlightened Witness
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A person who can be present with a feeling that was never met well the first time. She frames this as why the anxious route to healing cannot be walked alone: shame in particular does not survive being seen, and it is not survivable in isolation either.

  - derived_from → Brené Brown (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1206)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @1206s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1206

### Enmeshment
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Merging to the point where there is no clear line between two people. She distinguishes it sharply from intimacy: with no dividing line you have no vantage point from which to see the other person, so what feels like maximum closeness is actually the loss of the position closeness requires.

  - contrasts_with → Intimacy Requires Boundaries (https://youtu.be/GGEty6uo9Nc?t=138)

### Equally Comfortable In And Out Of A Relationship
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

A preference either way is fine; what marks security is that the sense of self does not change much between the two, and that being partnered does not require hiding any part of it. Priebe adds the practical consequence — secure people compromise, but choose relationships where the compromises improve the life, and leave early when the values plainly do not match rather than spending years on it.

### Expectation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Something you want another person to do. She is emphatic that these are not the problem — relationships run on them — but that they only function once both people have explicitly agreed. An expectation held privately and enforced silently produces exactly the frustration people mistake for a boundary being violated.

### External Locus Of Control
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The state of having no reliable way back to equilibrium that does not run through another person. She frames self-regulation as its remedy and describes it less as a technique than as a relationship with yourself — one where you are accountable to, trust, and respect the person doing the regulating.

  - contrasts_with → Self-Regulation (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=441)

### False Attribution
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A feeling that arrived earlier and unnoticed finds a plausible cause later in the day and fastens onto it. Her worked example runs from an unflattering photo in the morning to a partner's harmless like in the afternoon — on an ordinary day a flicker of irritation, on this one apparent proof. The logic can be wrong while the feeling is entirely real, and usually old.

### Fearful-Avoidance Is Not Anxious Plus Avoidant
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe calls this the single biggest misunderstanding in attachment theory. Having both anxious and avoidant traits does not make you fearful-avoidant, because everybody has both. What makes the style its own thing is a chronic disorientation about direction — am I going toward love or toward independence — combined with distrust of yourself and of everyone else at the same time.

### Feelings Are Data, Not Noise
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The stance that emotion should be subtracted from a decision because it is irrational. Priebe's objection is practical rather than moral: people behave emotionally, so a model that omits emotion predicts badly. Removing feelings from the equation does not produce a cleaner answer, it produces a blind spot in the answer.

### Fighting Fair
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Not an absence of conflict — she is clear that conflict is a healthy part of living alongside someone. What changes is that it becomes bearable. Neither person feels the whole relationship riding on this argument, so it can wait: both can cool down, think, and come back to it as two people against the problem rather than against each other.
