### First-Time Vulnerability Raises The Stakes
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Doing something for the first time — admitting you hurt someone, expressing anger, asking for something — costs far more than it looks like from outside, because the skin under that dressing has been covered for decades. So an imperfect response lands twice as hard, and the partner usually has no idea a threshold was crossed at all. Priebe's caution is that the expectation of a perfect reply is quietly unrealistic.

### Flexible Responsiveness
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

The payoff of having been responded to flexibly: more than one setting. Space for someone who needs space, reassurance for someone who needs reassurance, rather than one strategy applied to everyone. Each insecure style, by contrast, learned a single response system and runs it regardless of who is in front of them.

### Flight Is Also Enmeshment
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Avoidant people often claim other people's moods do not affect them, and Priebe's correction is precise: the moods affect them heavily and trigger flight rather than fight. Wanting out of the room is a physiologically aroused state, not a neutral one. So the avoidant is as entangled in the other person's emotion as the anxious partner — the difference is the direction of travel.

### Getting Needs Met Without Stating Them
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's compact definition of an insecure strategy: whatever you learned to do to get a need met without saying what the need is. The secure alternative is not a personality trait but an expectation — that stating it plainly will work — which holds because secure people mostly end up with people for whom it does.

### Grief Postponed, Not Avoided
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

After a breakup the avoidant machinery reports that nothing is wrong: it meant little, I am fine, I am strong. Then a crisis or a chance meeting arrives and the whole thing lands at once. Priebe traces the deficit to the original wound — the source of the pain was the attachment figure, so the pain had to be concealed from the only person who could have helped process it, and grieving was never learned.

### Guilt Versus Shame
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Guilt says I made a mistake; shame says I am one. Priebe notes the distinction is not universally agreed among theorists, and argues it matters specifically for attachment work because the two feelings move you in opposite directions — one toward the person you affected, one away from everyone.

### Handing Over The Finished Solution
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Believing the partner is not competent to help means never bringing them an unfinished problem — so the work is done alone and delivered as a conclusion. Priebe describes a partner who, after their first argument, produced a long letter explaining why he needed to step well back; her reply was, why not just talk about it and find a new balance. He looked at her as though she were speaking another language, and then they did exactly that.

### Healing Is Not Swinging To The Other Pole
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A guardrail she states explicitly at the close. If you are anxiously attached, the goal is not to go stoic and stop expressing anything — that is trading one insecure adaptation for the other. The target is the middle: emotion and reason both online, and interdependence rather than either codependence or counter-dependence.

### Healthy Dependency
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Total dependency is a problem; so is refusing to rely on anyone for anything. Priebe puts security in the middle: trusting people to do what they said, outsourcing accordingly, and renegotiating when it stops working. It rests on explicit agreements and on taking people at face value about what they can and cannot do — which does not prevent being let down, only makes it legible when it happens.

### History Not Ideals
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Your stated criteria come from the conscious mind; who you actually choose comes from underneath it. So the reliable evidence about what you are looking for is the pattern across the people you have picked, not the description you would give of your ideal.

### Holding Both Programs
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

What distinguishes the secure version. The threat response is not absent — the same costs get logged — but it runs alongside the appreciation instead of replacing it, which is what makes an actual negotiation possible.

### How Common Each Style Is
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Roughly half to sixty per cent of people are securely attached; anxious and avoidant each account for something near twenty per cent; fearful-avoidant is the rarest by a wide margin. Priebe cites the base rates specifically as a check on self-typing — the styles people most often claim are not the ones most people have.

### How Is This Adaptive In Our Dynamic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Insecure couples argue about who is right; secure ones have a working sense of context. Priebe's replacement question, asked together: how could this behaviour be adaptive inside the relationship we have built? Explosions may be what a person resorts to when the low-volume version is never integrated. Withdrawal may be what happens when parts of someone get quietly declined every time they arrive.

### Hyper-Awareness Of Power Dynamics
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A running background calculation in every relationship — friendship, work, romance — of what each person wants and what each has to withhold. Priebe notes it usually never surfaces as a thought; it shows up as who you can relax around. Attraction with uncertain reciprocity is uncomfortable for exactly this reason: you want their approval and they do not need yours, so the position has to be improved before anything can be risked.

### I Am Okay, You Are Okay
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The secure position, and she gives it a precise content rather than leaving it as a slogan: the assumption that everyone is behaving reasonably given what they have been through. Someone can be plainly not okay and still be intelligible — which is what stops their state from being read as illogical simply because it is not yours.

### Identity Separate From The Reaction Pattern
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The shift from experiencing a reaction as evidence about who you are to experiencing it as something running in you. She flags it as unusually load-bearing for fearful-avoidant people, whose default reading is that they are simply bad or incapable of love rather than conditioned — and it is the move that makes the rest of the work survivable.

### Impact Regardless Of Intent
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The capacity to hold that someone may have wanted things to be otherwise and that you were left unprotected anyway. Avoidant recall tends to run the two together, so a good explanation for why something happened is taken as evidence that it did no harm.

### Insatiable Anger As A Trauma Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A test Priebe uses on her own anger: if the problem in front of you were solved right now, would the anger stop? If not, it is not a response to this situation, and expressing it here will not discharge it. She treats that as the marker separating a trauma trigger from genuine present-tense anger, which is worth expressing and does resolve.

*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The secure form, and in the DMM the reason its secure category is called balanced: emotion informs what to do and reasoning informs what the feeling means, both online at once rather than in alternation.

### Integration, Not Addition
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Why this style's blind spot is structurally unlike the other two. Avoidant patterning is missing emotional information and anxious patterning is missing the analytic kind, so each has a side to develop. Fearful-avoidant has both already — and can only run one at a time. The work is not acquiring anything, it is using both at once, which is exactly what secure people do when they decide which to weight in a given moment.

### Interdependence Versus Codependence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The line she draws at the end: two people who can each hold themselves and choose to lean on one another are interdependent. Two people looking to each other for everything are not intimate but dependent — she calls it an addiction to being regulated by someone else rather than closeness.

### Internal Working Model
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The template for what relationships are and what you must do to get needs met, laid down before roughly age three when the brain is wiring fastest. It is not a memory but an expectation, and it is self-confirming: what you expect of people is largely what you go on to find.

### Intimacy Requires Boundaries
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her central reframe here: noticing where you end and someone else begins is not an obstacle to intimacy, it is the precondition for it. Only from a separate position can you understand what things are like for another person as distinct from what they are like for you — which is what seeing someone actually consists of.

### Intimacy Without Compromise
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant is most themselves alone and can stay single a long time, then wants the emotional closeness of a committed relationship without surrendering any control over their routines, interests or direction. Priebe's contrast is with the secure position: knowing what you want, and choosing to give some of it up because sharing a life averages out better than not.

### It Does Not Occur To Them
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A correction she is insistent about. Avoidant regulation is not someone feeling the pull to call a friend and refusing it — that description fits anxious or fearful-avoidant patterning resisting itself. Here the option simply does not present itself, which is why encouragement to reach out so often lands as noise.

  - contrasts_with → I Can Only Feel Better Through Someone Else (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=96)

### Knowing The Mechanism
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her answer to why understanding the origin matters at all, given that understanding changes nothing by itself. Without knowing where an impulse comes from you cannot anticipate it, so change has to be attempted blind and in the moment. Knowing the mechanism is what makes it possible to tell when the old response no longer fits the situation.

  - part_of → Not Your Fault, But Your Responsibility (https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=601)

  - derived_from → Gabor Maté (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=60)

### Limerence
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Believing the version of someone you assembled, in the face of evidence about the actual person. She quotes an observation that a crush is really a shortage of information — everyone fills the gaps, and the difference is whether the filling survives contact with facts.

  - source: Anxious Attachment: 3 Early Signs Of Healing @206s — https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=206

### Look At The Motivation, Not The Behaviour
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The rule Priebe says she has re-recorded this video repeatedly to get right. Every style borrows behaviour from every other: anxious people feel avoidant in the wrong relationship, avoidant people feel anxious about losing the one arrangement that lets them function as they prefer, secure people feel both when the situation warrants. Typing by behaviour, or even by feeling, gets you nowhere. The motivation underneath is the only thing that separates them.

  - mirrors → Same Behaviour, Opposite Motivation (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=60)

  - contrasts_with → Mistyping Into The Middle (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=30)

### Looking For A Parent, Not A Partner
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's account of why the pairing is so reliable. A good parent does not burden a small child with their problems, so the avoidant's aura of having nothing going on reads, to an anxious nervous system, as exactly the figure it has been looking for — more so than a secure person visibly working through their own material. The problem is that the parent is not a parent and has no intention of endlessly meeting needs.

  - part_of → We Seek What Is Familiar, Not What Is Healthiest (https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=180)

### Love Addiction And Detox
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's account of the fearful-avoidant cycle in the language of addiction: hooked despite knowing it is bad, then out and genuinely sober for a long stretch, then the thought that a relationship could be handled casually now — and back in. She distinguishes it from the anxious version, which craves the same drug without the adverse reaction, and notes that substance problems are common at both avoidant ends for the same reason.

  - mirrors → Time Alone That Is Not Healing (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=2270)

### Love Is The Medicine
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

With a compromised system, love does what the missing immunity cannot — it lets you function in a way you cannot manage alone. Secure people need it too and have it circulating already, through friendships and family they can reach for. The anxious version is desperation, because the dose is doing structural work, and the supplier is a single person.

### Making A Wrong Relationship One You Fit
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The cost of the whole tactical repertoire, stated plainly: if you will use every available means to keep someone present who does not authentically want to be, you succeed in making a relationship that is wrong for you into one you are well adapted to. The adaptation is real. So is the wrongness.

### Meaningful Goals And Collaboration
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Setting a goal that means something needs both faculties: the emotional one that knows what speaks to you, and the practical one that knows what makes sense. Priebe's marker is not that secure people never get this wrong, but that they do not have a lifelong structural weakness at either end — they can direct their own life and merge it with someone else's, and count both kinds of goal as real.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=1150)

### Mentalizing
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

Holding that another person's mind runs on different contents than your own — that something can be fine by you and not fine by them. It begins coming online around age four and keeps developing for life. Priebe's point is that guilt depends on it, which is why guilt is the later and more elaborate of the two feelings.

  - part_of → Attunement (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=350)

### Meta-Feelings About The Oscillation
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Fearful-avoidance is not only anxious triggers plus avoidant triggers. Because the system keeps switching, each state passes judgment on the other: the deactivated self is ashamed of what the activated self felt and said, and the activated self feels guilty about the distance the deactivated self wanted. Priebe treats this second layer as the distinctively fearful-avoidant part.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/QrhIWeLBkDQ?t=60)
  - part_of → Holding Both Programs (https://youtu.be/QrhIWeLBkDQ?t=180)

### Missing The Off Switch
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious counterpart. The pain registers fully; what is missing is the mechanism that ends it. Priebe's image is a stubbed toe that keeps hurting, harder and harder, until somebody else arrives to stop it — at which point wanting someone permanently within reach stops looking like insecurity and starts looking like a reasonable precaution.

  - mirrors → Dulled Pain Receptors (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=940)
  - part_of → Pain Is The Central Axis (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=950)

### Mistyping Into The Middle
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Fearful-avoidant is the category people place themselves in when they can see both anxious and avoidant behaviour in themselves but cannot yet tell the two apart. Secure people land there too, because a secure person does feel anxious when there is something to be anxious about. The discriminator is not the mix of behaviours but whether they fire when the situation warrants them.

  - contrasts_with → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=165)

### Mutual Trust
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Standing on two legs rather than one. Both people know where they stand — barring something extreme, nobody is leaving — and both know they would survive it if they did. Her image is a bird untroubled by the branch, because what it is relying on is its own wings.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=292)
  - contrasts_with → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=292)

### Navigating By Rules Instead Of Attunement
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Where the glue between people was never shared feeling, a child builds a rulebook instead: if she looks happy this morning, approach; if not, keep clear. It works, so it generalises — behaviour observed, patterns learned, risk of rejection minimised. The blindspot is not the method's accuracy but its omission: nothing in it involves being in emotional contact with anyone.

  - originates_in → Subtle Discomfort At Negative Emotion (https://youtu.be/TOGI3Zi7aX8?t=900)

### Needing The Medicine And Allergic To It
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A severely compromised system and an allergy to the only treatment. Priebe adds the detail that makes it worse: the painkillers do not hold for the fearful-avoidant the way they do for the dismissive. So the need surfaces anyway, the dose is taken, the reaction follows, and there is no version of the arrangement that works.

  - part_of → The Emotional Immune System (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1800)

### Needing The Person You Are Angry At
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

At the top of the scale the fearful-avoidant system runs two incompatible programmes at once: get the anger out, and get this person on side so they will help bring me down again. Priebe traces it to never having learned down-regulation from anger in childhood — the only route back to baseline runs through someone else, and the only person available is the one being shouted at.

### Negative View Of Self, Positive View Of Others
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The classic anxious position, and the engine behind idealisation. Reading it as seeing the best in someone is the flattering version; the mechanism is closer to assigning qualities you need them to have, then meeting the real person as a disappointment.

  - contrasts_with → I Am Okay, You Are Okay (https://youtu.be/ahzCikYhM_o?t=970)

### No Stable Centre Of Gravity
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe puts numbers on it. The anxious person sits at roughly eighty per cent outside themselves and twenty per cent grounded; the avoidant runs the inverse; the fearful-avoidant hovers near the middle with no settled answer. Hence the practical paralysis — no stable view on whether to invest in relationships or in self-work, because whichever you chose last week was chosen by a different configuration.

  - part_of → Where Your Centre Of Gravity Sits (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=1200)

### Nobody Is Required To Give You Their Attention
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A child has a survival claim on a parent's attention, and the tactics that enforce that claim are legitimate at four. An adult partner has no such obligation: they may decide not to care, not to love you, and to walk away in the moment you need them. Priebe states it without softening, because the tactics only make sense while the claim is assumed.

  - part_of → Regressing To Child And Parent In Conflict (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=640)

### Nobody Made That Experience Matter
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A phrase Priebe took from a speaker at a workshop, describing a close family member dying in childhood: nobody made that experience matter. It is the caregiver's job to see the child's interior and connect it to what has happened — you feel grief, you feel loss, those are the right responses to this. Where that does not happen, the feeling arrives with no place to sit.

### Not A Personality Type
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Why the usual personality-system habits do not transfer. Those frameworks assume the type is fixed, so the useful move is to celebrate your quirks and work with your natural energy. Attachment styles are changeable, and what is dominant in an insecure one is mostly the part that is not working — so treating it as an identity to embrace inverts the point of knowing it.

### Not Taking Moods Personally
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

There are two ways to take a mood personally: reading it as rejection, or being irritated that someone is displaying what you have learned to suppress. Priebe's secure version is neither — curiosity at a slight distance, an offer of help if it is within reach, and otherwise carrying on, because their state genuinely is not about you.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=220)
  - part_of → Differentiation (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=250)

### Not Your Fault, But Your Responsibility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The principle she puts at the centre of the whole endeavour, and the one most often split in half. People collapse the two clauses together — if I did not cause it, then fixing it is not mine to do — and the framework becomes an explanation for staying as you are. Both halves have to be held at once: you did not choose the patterning, and you are the only one who can change it.

  - source: How Not To Use Attachment Theory @481s — https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=481

### One Root, Many Symptoms
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Procrastinating at work, picking fights, eating when you are not hungry — apparently unrelated until you notice they all run when you feel insecure. Priebe's argument for the slowness of stage two is that noticing across enough areas is what lets you find the root, and that solving the root retires the symptoms without having to be fought one at a time.

### Openness Without Self-Protection
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious imbalance. She is careful to name the strength first and rate it highly: a real openness to being taught and changed by loving someone, which she says is genuinely unavailable to much of the avoidant spectrum and is required for a secure partnership. Unbalanced it leaves a person entirely undefended — her image is an infant lying open-armed in a cot, an energy that works precisely because someone else is doing the protecting.

### Others Meet You As Deeply As You Have Met Yourself
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe names this as the most profound shift of her own attachment work: going from a bodily certainty of existential aloneness to a bodily belief that she could be known. The order mattered. Uncovering the no-go areas in her own psyche was what made it possible to communicate herself to other people at all — a thing she had previously experienced as impossible rather than difficult.

### Over- And Under-Taking Responsibility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Activated, the fearful-avoidant is owed things and the partner is failing them. Deactivated, they cannot reach the emotion they were in, look at their own conduct through a cold analytic lens and conclude they must be the abusive one. Priebe is careful on both sides: they genuinely can be, as any insecure style can, and the deactivated verdict is not more accurate for being calmer. The disorientation is the diagnostic feature.

### Overwhelm And Judgment Are The Boundary Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

An avoidant system does not present a clear sense of what is needed — it presents overload, distress, and a judgement about the other person. Priebe reframes all three as the same message: a boundary is required here. The judgement is not a verdict on them, it is the notification.

### Pain Hidden From Yourself
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her correction of the usual stereotype, and an important one: this is not someone concealing pain from other people. When it reaches conscious awareness they process it about as well as anyone. The trouble is that it largely does not arrive — frustration and contempt surface in its place, and once out of the activating moment the memory loses most of its emotional charge. Better for analysis, useless for learning.

  - contrasts_with → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=602)

### Pain Is The Central Axis
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's reframe of the whole system. Attachment is usually described as how you relate to other people; she argues the load-bearing variable underneath is how you process emotional pain. Nobody is exempt from it — the difference between the styles is what happens once it arrives, and most of the outward behaviour follows from that.

### Painkillers Instead Of Medicine
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Unable to take the medicine, the avoidant takes analgesics: overwork, drink, substances, food, compulsive escape into fiction. Priebe's objection runs through an Advil advert she saw — pain says you can't, Advil says you can — which she reads as exactly wrong. Pain is the indicator, not the problem. Silence it and you keep using the injured arm.

### Parallel Support
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her picture of what adult intimacy looks like: two people moving alongside each other, each responsible for their own healing, offering support across that separation. The alternative she contrasts it with is two people facing each other and treating the other as the solution — which is the arrangement the fantasy is built around.

### People-Pleasing Is A Barrier To Intimacy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious system reports that accommodating will bring you closer. It does the opposite: it deletes the interesting, differing parts of you and puts a reflection of the other person in their place. Nobody enters a relationship wanting themselves mirrored back. The more either person pleases, the less there is in the room to be close to.

### Phobia Of Inner Experiences
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Certain emotional states have no regulation attached to them, so the system redirects before they arrive. Priebe's examples are specific: anger begins in the body and a freeze response takes over; sadness begins and attention suddenly has to be somewhere else, online, researching, anywhere. It reads as distraction. It is a flight response, and the information in the feeling never lands.

### Powerless Over Others
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The premise Priebe rates as the single most useful thing an anxious-spectrum person can accept. If you truly could not influence what someone thinks or feels about you, the whole repertoire becomes pointless — and what appears in its place is the set of questions you have been avoiding: is this the right person, is this situation safe for me, what would a better option look like?

### Predictability Restores Calm
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Why a named time settles a nervous system that an open-ended promise cannot. Her analogy is a hungry child told repeatedly not yet, versus one told they will eat when you get home in three quarters of an hour — the second can wait, because the question has changed from whether to when.

  - contrasts_with → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=481)

### Presence And Curiosity Versus Strategy And Analysis
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A child who was met with presence and curiosity copies it: they meet people as blank slates and let what is unique to each connection emerge. A child who was not has to find another route, and the route available is analysis — working out in advance who this person is, what they would like, and who to be for them. Both feel like paying close attention. Only one is attending to the actual person.

### Projecting Your Own Remedy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Seeing a partner withdraw, the anxious system reads it through its own machinery: if I withdrew, it would be to draw someone closer — so they must need love. And so love is delivered, in quantity, to someone who was asking for space. Priebe names the trap: this is how you can give continuously, receive nothing back, and conclude you are being undervalued, while never once giving the thing that was wanted.

### Promises Made By A Self You Cannot Guarantee
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Commitments get made sincerely by one configuration and come due to another — the career built on emotional openness that becomes unbearable the week vulnerability is actually required, the resolution to be emotionally healthy that dissolves on the next activation. Priebe's point is that the resulting self-distrust is well-founded, and that awareness of the pattern makes decisions harder before it makes them easier.

### Protection And Comfort
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The two things attuned care supplies, and the distinction that organises the whole model. Protection resolves the cause so it is less likely to recur, and includes the unwelcome limits that prevent future pain; comfort meets the fact that some of it is hard regardless. Each insecure style turns out to have received one and not the other.

### Psychic Equivalence
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The assumption that the intensity of your feeling measures the badness of your situation. Priebe uses it to explain a pattern she sees constantly: an anxious person in an emotional flashback feels overwhelmingly awful, concludes the awfulness must be coming from the person in front of them, and reaches for toxic, gaslighter, narcissist. The positive version does the same work in reverse, and produces idealisation.

### Punishing Humility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A partner arrives with an apology and gets the other ten unaddressed items, or a speech about how unacceptable it all was. Understandable — humility from them is rare, so the window feels precious — and it reliably ensures the next one does not come. Priebe's wider version: an environment hostile to mistakes does not produce fewer mistakes, it produces less honesty about them.

### Rational And Emotional, But Never At Once
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant has access to distorted emotion like the anxious and distorted logic like the avoidant, and no integration between them. Priebe describes the effect on the people around them: a friend who can set out precisely why the relationship cannot work, and keeps choosing it — because the analysis was done deactivated and the decisions are made activated, and neither state can reach the other.

### Reading People Easily
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Having learned early that what people say is unreliable, the fearful-avoidant reads everything else — and gets genuinely good at it. Priebe knows one who became a world-class poker player on exactly that skill. What distinguishes it from anxious hypervigilance is comfort looking at their own manipulations, which makes other people's legible too. The blind spot is secure people, whose lack of strategy reads as a strategy being concealed.

### Realistic Cause And Effect
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

The secure position between the two distortions: neither authoring everything that happens to you nor being at the mercy of everyone else. It means checking whether you are being taken advantage of, setting boundaries where you are, and otherwise engaging in good faith.

The one she calls most important. Insecurity brings expectations a relationship cannot meet, and the relationship then buckles under them. Her image is hunting for milk in a hardware store — the disappointment is guaranteed by the premise, and no amount of effort inside the shop fixes it.

*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

When the connection feels threatened, the anxious system stops seeing another adult with needs of their own and starts seeing a parent — someone to be placated by abandoning your position, or fought hard to be heard at all. Priebe is clear that conflict with people you love is dysregulating for anyone; the tell is the shift in who you think you are talking to.

### Regulating With The Idea Of Each Other
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's account of why insecure couples produce enormous fights: both are relating to the picture of the other person, and to a picture of how a relationship should go, rather than to what is in front of them. Attunement is the corrective not because it prevents disagreement but because it catches divergence early — a chasm cannot open quietly between two people who are actually in the present moment together.

### Relationships As Resource
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Seeing a relationship as something that supplies you rather than only draws on you. Until it is a resource, the sacrifices it asks for have no rationale and will read as pure loss.

### Relief Mistaken For Joy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her central move in this video, built on a pair of images. Live with a low-grade headache long enough and painkillers start to feel sublime — but the best available state was never the pill, it was not having the headache, and you have no way to tell the difference from inside. Live hungry and food becomes the whole world; eat properly and your attention is free for everything else. The highs of insecure attachment are relief from a chronic background of not being good enough, and relief is temporary by construction.

### Repressed Emotion Breaks Through Harder
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

An anxiously attached person is in continuous contact with their subtler feelings; a fearful-avoidant is not, and may go through a day unaware of how much is running underneath. Priebe's observation is that the emotion which does break through can therefore land harder than the anxious version of the same feeling, precisely because everything below it stayed down.

### Repression Versus Suppression
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Suppression is knowing a need is there, choosing to set it down for now, and intending to come back to it — renting while you save for the house you know you want. Repression puts the need somewhere you cannot find it, so you keep moving and feel vaguely wrong without ever locating what you are missing. Both look like going without; only one leaves the need retrievable.

### Resolution Versus Regulation
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Mid-argument, the question worth asking is which goal is running. Advocating a need and hearing theirs is one thing; getting them to make you feel better is another, and the second quietly replaces the first without announcing itself. It sounds like: how do I get them to see how much pain I am in. The points you came in with are usually the casualty.

### Responding To The Past In The Present
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Meeting a current situation with emotions belonging to an old one — furious that a partner cannot read a need that went unmet in childhood, or that they failed to give space you never asked for. Priebe's point is that most insecurely attached people do this continuously while taking the reaction as an accurate reading of the present, and that catching it is the whole of the first step.

### Rigidity Is Adaptive At Seventy Per Cent
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Without reliable feedback about what keeps you in connection, anything that works seven times in ten deserves to be run every single time — it is the best available bet. That is why insecure relating goes rigid, and why the other three times in ten keep producing the same damage. Priebe's point is that the rigidity is intelligent, and that it stops being intelligent once feedback becomes available.

### Safety Is What Allows You To Criticise Your Parents
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Securely attached people frequently type themselves as insecure, because a settled nervous system can afford to look squarely at what a parent got wrong. The avoidant adaptation runs the other way — the childhood has to be described as fine. So an unflattering account of your parents is weak evidence of insecure attachment, and a flawless one is weak evidence of secure attachment.

### Same Behaviour, Opposite Motivation
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Storming out, picking a fight and threatening to end it appear in both the anxious and the avoidant repertoire, and they mean opposite things. Run as protest, the behaviour is a bid for pursuit — the hoped-for outcome is being followed. Run as deactivation, the hoped-for outcome is distance. Read the wanted result, not the action, or you will type yourself and your partner wrongly.

*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

What a partner is for in the secure version: somewhere to bring a difficulty and be supported through it, not somewhere to hand it over. The problems of feeling stable and worth something stay yours to work on; the relationship is where that work is shared rather than outsourced.

Get the commitment, then work out the rest. ### Secure People Feel Most Accurately
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

A claim that cuts against the stereotype: the secure style feels emotion in its purest form. The anxious person feels very intensely and often inaccurately, half in a fantasy. The avoidant registers far less than is actually running, storing the rest out of awareness. Grief is grief for the secure person and loneliness is loneliness — painful, undisguised, and not accompanied by panic in either direction.

### Security Changes The Power Dynamic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A secure relationship has a roughly even power balance, so moving toward one means the existing balance goes. If you want your partner more independent, you will be the one reaching out, planning, fitting into their life. If you want them more emotional, you will be holding raw dysregulated material from someone who has suppressed it for decades. Priebe's rule: be ready for the side effects, or your system will quietly push them back into the old role.

### Seeing Yourself As The Common Denominator
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant does eventually notice they are the constant across their relationships — which is more than most insecure styles manage — and then draws the wrong inference from it, because they have no account of their own mechanism. Priebe's counter-claim is that what looks like bad character is early wiring for self-protection, and that the well-meaning part underneath is what healing is grown from.

### Self-Abandoning Moves Feel Vulnerable
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Fawning, dressing a want as a principle, and turning the volume up on the pain all feel like vulnerability in the moment and are the opposite: each one manages the other person's response. The vulnerable act is stating what is true at the size it actually is and letting them choose freely whether they want to be there.

### Self-Esteem Versus Shame
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Self-esteem is holding that you are well-meaning and that you get things wrong, both at once — not the conviction that you never do, which she distinguishes sharply as something else. Someone shame-bound believes they are fundamentally a mistake, and can carry a strong ego with no self-esteem at all, which is why they cannot afford to be wrong about anything.

### Self-Protection Lets Your Partner Be Human
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Permanent openness means being permanently receptive to whatever the other person is carrying, so a short reply or a distracted evening lands as a verdict. Priebe's point is that this quietly requires your partner never to be off — and that the alternative is the skill avoidant people over-develop and secure people hold at the right amount: sitting with someone in their own difficulty and knowing it is not about you.

### Self-Regulation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Bringing yourself back to equilibrium without another person doing it for you. Security requires both this and co-regulation, chosen according to circumstance; each insecure style tends to have practised one and skipped the other.

### Sensitivity In The True Sense
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe stops to disambiguate the word. She does not mean becoming easily wounded or more defended. She means literally being in your senses: noticing what is happening in reality right now, how it is landing in your body, and what is shifting in the other person's energy as the conversation moves. It is the same faculty a dancer uses to follow a partner's small changes.

  - part_of → Attunement (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1750)

### Separating The Feeling From The Action
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

After a rupture the instinct is to disown the whole episode, feeling included. Priebe insists on the split: apologise for how you expressed it and for whatever was unkind or out of integrity, and keep the need that produced it, which still has to be resolved somewhere. The feeling is a normal consequence of being alive; the action is what accountability attaches to.

### Separation Between Parent And Child
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The condition that makes containment possible: the child's emotional range is not experienced as a statement about the parent. Anger can be met and worked with rather than taken personally, which is what lets it be helped rather than suppressed.

  - part_of → Differentiation (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=242)

### Shame-Bound Emotion
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

An emotion that was met with disgust or rejection often enough that having it, and especially showing it, comes to feel shameful in itself. The feeling and the shame arrive fused.

  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @718s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=718

### Signal And Muddle
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Terms Priebe takes from a friend, for the two halves of a projection. The signal is the true thing inside what is being said; the muddle is everything inaccurate around it. "You don't care about me" is muddle to the person receiving it and signal to the person saying it. Neither of them is wrong, and nothing resolves until both are willing to dig for the kernel together rather than argue whose reading wins.

### Single Calm, Partnered Turbulent
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The avoidant spectrum is often steadier single than partnered, because closeness is what brings the wounds to the surface. The anxious spectrum runs the opposite way — being alone is when the material arrives. Priebe notes the practical consequence: the avoidant's post-breakup relief is real and is not evidence that the relationship meant nothing.

### Social Referencing
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

How a child learns to categorise its own inner states: something happens, and it checks the faces around it. Frightened, but everyone is eating popcorn — so this kind of frightening is safe. The mechanism only works if the room's response maps onto the child's interior. In an avoidant family where the grief is felt and not shown, the child concludes the grief itself is the wrong thing to be feeling.

### Somatic Strategy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The attachment strategy is laid down in the body before language exists. If extreme distress met disgust or a caregiver going distant, the body begins suppressing extreme distress. If only extreme distress got a response, the body begins amplifying discomfort. Priebe's emphasis is that nobody selected this — the secure belief that showing a feeling at its true volume brings appropriate care is simply not what your tissue learned.

### Some Needs Are Shared Work
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant default is that any need brought to you is excessive and belongs to the person carrying it. Priebe's target is narrower than it sounds: ninety per cent of your needs really are yours to handle, and ten per cent are relationship business that two people put on the table and work out. Recognising that category exists at all is most of the change.

### Steady Baseline
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Being alright as a constant rather than an event. Not overwhelming, which is why it can be mistaken for dullness, and precisely why it is not chased. Her contrast is standing on solid ground versus standing on a summit that might give way: what is real stays steady whether things are going well or badly, and only a fantasy that happens to match reality has to be defended against changing.

### Suppressing Anger Suppresses Boundaries
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The part of you that registers a line being crossed and the part that gets angry are the same part. Put anger under a general ban — as an unsafe childhood teaches — and the boundary-setting faculty goes down with it. Priebe treats boundaries as what keeps the alive, engaged parts of a person present inside a relationship, so losing them is not a small administrative cost.

### Talking It Out Directly
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

The drama triangle is what you do when a need cannot be stated outright. Secure people are not carrying shame about having feelings and needs that differ from someone else's, so the direct conversation is simply available — say how you feel, ask how they feel, look for a resolution. Priebe is clear this does not mean it always works, only that it is not frightening to attempt.

### The Anger Scale
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Rating anger one to ten and noticing where you actually speak. Priebe's own pattern was silence at everything up to eight and then a nine or ten, at which point self-regulation is no longer available and the conversation cannot go well. The workable band is low — around two or three, when the feeling is small enough to state calmly and the problem is small enough to fix.

### The Averages Come Out The Same
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Looking back at a three-year on-and-off relationship, Priebe worked out that the total time she spent alone versus with her partner came out at roughly what a secure couple would have anyway. The difference was distribution: secure people notice they need space on a Tuesday and take it, while enmeshment followed by a breakup takes the same solitude in one indigestible piece, at the cost of the relationship.

### The Avoidant Audition
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Avoidant courtship runs long and reads as evaluation rather than falling: how does this person behave here, what do they like, what do they earn, do I respect it — and a firm boundary set partly to see whether it is honoured. Attraction is one of ten or twenty inputs. Priebe is careful that this is not absence of feeling; it is feeling at low volume under a permanent sedative.

### The Avoidant Differentiation Blindspot
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Differentiation is two things: knowing where you end and someone else begins, and understanding how the two of you act on each other. Avoidant patterning tends to have the first and lack the second — so a partner's difficulty reads as entirely theirs. Priebe adds the mirror-image cost: not noticing how others affect you leaves you assuming everyone else operates in a sealed compartment too.

### The Balanced View Of People
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Ask a secure person about a parent or a partner and you get neither idealisation nor prosecution — the quirks that irritate them, and the circumstances that made someone unable to show up. Priebe names it as the strongest tell of earned security: someone who was genuinely abused and can now hold what happened both emotionally and rationally, without needing a villain, and without saying it was acceptable.

### The Best I Have Found So Far
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A few unsatisfying relationships later, the old one starts to look like the high-water mark. Priebe's reading is that the search was constrained rather than exhausted — nothing better turned up partly because there is no life outside a relationship for a better partner to join. The test she offers is direct: would this person add to a life that is already good, or are they a raft in a sea you are drowning in?

### The Blame Flips With The State
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Activated, the worldview is I am not okay and you are, so the responsibility for fixing this is yours. Deactivated, it inverts: I am fine, you cannot manage yourself, so the responsibility is mine and I should audit my own conduct. Being thrown between the two is disorienting precisely because each position feels complete while you are in it.

### The Bowl And The Soup
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's image for the correction. The soup is plentiful and freely given; what differs is whether you arrived with a bowl. The anxious spectrum has no vessel and must stand under the ladle or borrow someone else's. The avoidant has the bowl but was once served something poisoned, so the soup gets carried around uneaten. In both cases supply was never the problem.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

If you want to end it but also want to stay friends, keep seeing them, keep them in reach — Priebe reads that as a signal you are not ready to leave. You are overwhelmed, and ending the relationship is the only route to space you have. The need is real; the instrument is wrong. What is missing is the ability to ask for autonomy while staying in.

### The Conscious Competence Model
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The four-stage frame she maps healing onto: running the pattern without seeing it, running it while seeing it, being able to do otherwise with deliberate effort, and finally doing otherwise without effort. Most early signs of change sit in the second and third stages, which is why they feel unimpressive from inside — awareness arrives long before ease does.

### The Deflated Wheel
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her frame for why reflection after a bad relationship so often fails. Reviewing what went wrong, we reach for the thing we already do well and do more of it — inflating a tyre that was half full while the flat one stays flat, because it sits in the blind spot. The result is a bike that steers only in circles. Each insecure style has a different over-used strength and a different missing one.

### The Distress Scale
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her central device here: put distress on a scale of one to ten and ask where a caregiver reliably stepped in. Infants cannot regulate themselves, so a parent effectively serves as the child's nervous system, and the level at which they intervened becomes the rulebook for what counts as distress worth attending to for the rest of that person's life.

  - part_of → Window Of Tolerance (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=244)

### The Drama Triangle
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A conflict model of three roles — victim, persecutor and saviour — that people rotate through during a dispute. Everyone occupies all three at times, but most have a preferred entry point, and one person taking a role pushes the other into one of the remaining two.

  - derived_from → Stephen Karpman (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=1)

### The Emotional Immune System
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Priebe's organising metaphor for the whole series. Security is a working immune system: bad things still happen, breakups still hurt, and you recover at an ordinary rate. It is not a life without difficulty — she is careful about that — it is the absence of a fundamentally distorted view of what relationships are. Insecure attachment is the compromised version of the same system.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=100)
  - mirrors → Steady Baseline (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=150)

### The Empowerment Dynamic
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The counterpart system, with a healthy role mirroring each of the triangle's three. What changes across all three is where the next move is expected to come from: the triangle waits on someone else, this one starts from what remains available to you.

  - source: Attachment Styles & The Drama Triangle (Part 1): Intro To The Drama Triangle @555s — https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=555

### The Exit Fantasy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Both anxious and fearful-avoidant drive the same road — my needs get met by someone else — but the fearful-avoidant reads every exit sign, believing the turn-off leads to a place where their own needs are permitted again. So the fantasy is not a scene in which the partner runs after them; it is the relationship genuinely over and life good afterwards. Believed long enough, the relationship becomes the explanation for everything missing.

### The Free-Alone-Or-Trapped-Together Dichotomy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The belief the fearful-avoidant most needs dismantled: that autonomy and connection are alternatives you pick between. Priebe's counter is that the freedom claimed by leaving — time alone, friendships, solo holidays, a normal degree of independence — is all available inside a relationship, and was only unavailable in the enmeshed family the belief came from.

### The Hostility Blindspot
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Adapting to a mildly hostile emotional environment means tuning out low-level hostility aimed at you — which reads, from inside, as resilience. The cost is a dulled sense of the hostility you emit. Priebe's point is that an anxious partner is exquisitely sensitive to contempt in tone and posture, so what looks like overreaction to your words is frequently an accurate reaction to something else entirely.

Measuring yourself against a standard of what someone lovable would be, and working toward it — with the standard moving as you approach. ### The Inner Secure Base
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

What actually changes with security, as distinct from what people hope changes. Problems do not stop arriving and you do not stop being wrong-footed by them. What you gain is somewhere to return to that is not contingent on how the current situation resolves — the full emotional range still available, without the desperation to have it settled by someone else.

### The Inner-Outer Feedback Loop
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Security runs a continuous cycle: share the inner world, get feedback, update. Without it there are two failure modes. Feel something strong with no obvious external cause and conclude you are irrational — the feeling goes underground taking its information with it. Or feel something strong and assign it to whatever is nearest, so someone must be behaving badly. Priebe's example of an inner world that stopped updating is a friend still talking about an ex a year on as though the breakup were last week.

### The Intimacy Desert
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's name for the fearful-avoidant's supply problem. One relationship holds all of the intimacy, and everything outside it is desert. She describes living inside a warm house surrounded by a frigid world, where the heating sometimes cut out. The codependency does not come from weakness of character — it comes from there being nowhere else to go.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=390)

### The Loaded Argument
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Why insecure conflict resists resolution. Her worked example is an argument about washing up in which one person is really arguing that they are worth loving and the other that they cannot be controlled. Settling who does the dishes is easy; settling a lifetime of wounding in one conversation is not, and the second is what is actually on the table.

### The Magical Future Fantasy
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A named feature of anxious attachment: a vivid picture of a future in which everything has come right — the family, the travelling, the ease — with no account of how anyone gets there from here. Priebe's correction is arithmetic. If conflict is unresolvable now, five years on it is unresolvable with children added, because the fantasy has no ground under it.

### The Mutual Hostage Situation
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Holding a negative view of self and of others at once produces a relationship the fearful-avoidant does not admire and cannot leave: they need someone to soothe the view of self, and their view of others means the partner is not respected or looked forward to. What holds it together is that each knows the other's worst material. Priebe notes it recurs across partners, because it is the intimacy itself that triggers the criticism.

### The Ninety-Ten Ratio
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Secure people are better at leaving relationships that do not meet their needs, and Priebe's explanation is unsentimental: having other options, they can see clearly. Noticing that ninety per cent of the regulating is theirs and ten per cent is met, they read it as information about fit rather than as insult or injury — and act on it. Seeing your partner as the only route to relief is what removes that clarity.

### The Observing And Experiencing Selves
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The part that notices what is happening and the part that reacts before noticing is possible. Feelings arrive in the body ahead of the conscious mind, so there is little choice about having them — the choice lives entirely in what the observing self does next.

### The Premature Breakup
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

In an anxious-avoidant pairing neither person states needs or boundaries plainly, so unmet needs and unspoken expectations accumulate until someone — usually the avoidant-leaning one — ends it under overwhelm. The feelings are still there and the business is unfinished, which is exactly why the pair drifts back. The breakup solved the overwhelm and none of the causes.

### The Proximity-Seeking Blindspot
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Attachment is built partly by both people pursuing — making plans, making the other feel wanted, rearranging around them. The avoidant tendency is to let the other person do the fitting-in. Priebe's rule of thumb: how guarded you are sets how unbounded a partner you attract, because a secure person reads no room in your life and withdraws, while someone whose worth depends on your approval will step over their own limits to stay.

### The Relationship As Organising Principle
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

It is reasonable for a serious relationship to be one of the things your life orbits. The blindspot is how early that happens — three or four dates in, mood already keyed to their messages, life already rearranging. Priebe's objection is structural: two people with strong centres of gravity elsewhere have something to look into and learn about. Abandon yours and there is nothing to see.

### The Relationship With An Exit Strategy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant can be fully enmeshed — needs given up, life merged — while privately holding a date or a condition on which they leave. The exit is what makes the closeness survivable. From outside it looks like total commitment; the tolerance for it is being financed by the escape route nobody else knows about.

### The Rules You Think The Relationship Requires
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A set of rigid conditions learned early and now applied without inspection: I can never be angry with a partner. I must caretake at any cost. I cannot put anything between us. They kept you safe once, which is why they feel non-negotiable. Followed long enough, they hollow you out — which is why the avoidant spectrum often feels more alive single than partnered.

The standard attachment-community claim that insecure people wrongly believe love is scarce and must cling to whoever currently offers it. Priebe accepts half of it and rejects the other half: the estimate of how many people could love you is too low, but the sense that love is harder to come by for you than for others is tracking something real.

### The Second Level Of The Feeling
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

First level: irritated, overloaded. Second level: I cannot handle this much emotion, and that makes me uncomfortable, inadequate, possibly frightened. Underneath sits a need — time to think, or someone to ask the right questions. Priebe's point is that only the second level and the need are communicable; the first level on its own gives the other person nothing to work with.

### The Secure Person Is Less Vulnerable
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The counterintuitive comparison Priebe puts to the avoidant reader. A secure person is less exposed to hurt, because they have people who help them recover from it; less exposed to betrayal, because they engage honestly with others doing the same; less exposed to rejection, because they can be seen whole rather than through a persona. The wall is not the safer position, it only feels like it.

### The Shared Middle Ground
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The place a mixed-attachment conflict can end: accurate emotional information and an accurate account of events on the table at the same time. Reaching it costs both people their defence — the anxious partner has to say plainly what happened, the avoidant partner has to accept the feeling as real before the sequence is settled. Neither concession works unless the other is made.

### The Shock Experiment
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Participants awaiting intermittent electric shocks were measured with and without another person present holding their hand. Anxious participants' stress fell when someone was there; avoidant participants' stress rose. Priebe reports it from Attached or The Attachment Effect and reads the avoidant result as the cost of having a second nervous system to manage.

### The Soulmate Fantasy In Three Versions
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Anxious: someone who loves the flaws away and completes a life. Avoidant: someone who has a normal relationship with you while staying perfectly regulated, never unreasonable, never asking for anything unwanted, and intuiting everything so nothing needs saying. Fearful-avoidant: a soulmate who exists, for whom you are not yet good enough, so you develop quietly until you qualify. Priebe calls all three bogus in the same breath.

### The Still-Face Experiment
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A caregiver is asked to hold a blank, unresponsive face at an infant. The infant escalates through a ladder of bids — crying, then charming, then throwing things — because it has no other way to restore contact. Priebe uses it as the clearest picture of where protest behaviour comes from: not manipulation, but a repertoire being run through in order.

### The Threat Was Also The Refuge
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The other account: at the age the strategy formed, the source of danger and the only available protection were the same person. The system cannot resolve approach against withdrawal, so it freezes, then alternates according to how the caregiver is behaving that hour. Priebe is emphatic that this is the correct response to that situation, not a malfunction.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A response that is wildly out of scale with the incident and exactly in scale with the arrears. Priebe's point is that this is what makes the retrospective self-verdict so wrong: every one and two that went into the total was valid when it was felt. ### The Unconscious Payoff
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The step Priebe rates most important and least expected: work out what need the behaviour you want gone is currently meeting. Constant screaming matches can be what holds a couple together if it is the only relationship model either of them has; explosive fights can be the only route by which your needs ever get seen. Where there is a payoff, dropping the behaviour meets fierce resistance from a part of you that is not in the conversation.

### There Is Always A Rationality Underneath
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe is unusually firm here: if someone's behaviour looks irrational to you, that is a statement about the depth of your understanding, not about them. Given their history, their biology and what is happening around them, what they are doing makes sense from where they stand. This does not make it right or well-informed — it makes it explicable, which is the only thing you can work with.

### Time Alone That Is Not Healing
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Out of a relationship the fearful-avoidant runs the avoidant programme and it works — comfortable, self-sufficient, apparently doing the work. Priebe's warning is that minimising your own and everyone else's emotions is not self-soothing, and it holds only until something genuinely painful arrives. Then, with no real regulation skills built, the return is straight back into enmeshment.

### Toughness Requires Isolation
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

If vulnerability has to stay unreachable, relationships have to stay shallow, because give-and-take needs you to know and be able to say what you need. Priebe reads toughness as a permanently activated state — on guard, because nothing else will catch you — and strength as a calm one, because the load is spread across enough people and systems that no single failure is fatal.

### Toughness Versus Strength
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Attachment communities frequently read the avoidant style as the emotionally strongest, because it does not visibly suffer or ask. Priebe's counter is that it is the most durable, not the strongest: toughness absorbs pain without processing it, strength feels the appropriate thing at the appropriate time and makes a better decision because of it. The strongest style is secure.

### Trauma Disrupts Meaning, Neglect Prevents It
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's cleanest distinction, taken from a joke she saw about someone with complex trauma listening to someone with single-incident trauma describe life before it — wait, you had a before? ### Trauma Fluency As A Bridge
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's argument for trauma work beyond symptom relief: it gives you words for your own history that you can hand to someone without feeling skinned in the process. Once the account can be contained and offered rather than exposed, connection stops requiring a matching history — which is what makes the world at large habitable rather than something to shelter from inside one relationship.

### Trust As Mutually Assured Vulnerability
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Believing people betray each other whenever it makes sense to, the unhealed fearful-avoidant does not look for warmth or kindness as evidence of safety. They look for structure: I know something equally damaging about you, or you like me appreciably more than I like you. Once the incentives are aligned so that hurting them would cost you, they relax — which is the closest this style comes to trusting anyone.

### Twenty Per Cent Compatible By Default
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's diagnosis of the avoidant dating pattern: fear of rejection means rarely pursuing anyone actually wanted, so the field narrows to whoever approaches — which is disproportionately people who cannot meet their own needs. The complaint about always dating people who need too much is therefore a report on a selection method, not on the world. Nobody is a hundred per cent match; eighty is available to someone who shows up.

### Two Ends Of The Avoidant Spectrum
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

At the mild end, negative emotion was merely unrewarding, and the adult reroutes to problem-solving without noticing. At the severe end it was dangerous, and the adult suppresses both unconsciously and deliberately, may resent other people's freedom to express, and can carry an ego about enduring without complaint — while almost never naming what was done to them as abuse.

### Types Of Intimacy Are Not Interchangeable
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Friendship intimacy, where you can be plainly imperfect. Romantic intimacy, including building a life alongside someone. Mentorship intimacy, one-directional, where you receive without reciprocating. Long-witness intimacy, where someone has watched you change over years. Priebe's argument is that several of these are mutually exclusive by structure, so routing them all through one partner is not demanding — it is impossible.

### Unconscious Competence
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The new response has become the default and no longer competes with the old one. Priebe describes it in concrete terms — safe in your own body, noticing feelings as they arrive, self-soothing without deciding to, reading trustworthiness without effortful analysis — and names it as the point at which the internal working model has actually changed rather than been overridden.

### Unconscious Incompetence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Knowing that relationships keep going wrong and not knowing why. Priebe's sharpest point about this stage is that you can already know your attachment style and still be in it: as long as the plan is for the other person to change, the problem has not been located yet.

### Unconscious Relationship Premise
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

What a relationship is for, as held below the stated version. Two people can share an explicit intention word for word and hold incompatible premises underneath it. Security is largely the condition of these two being the same thing; insecurity is the gap, which stays invisible until conflict brings the lower one forward to argue on your behalf.

### Unintegrated Logic And Emotion
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The Dynamic Maturation Model's account of this pattern: both a reasoning strategy and an emotional strategy are available, but only one runs at a time. Decisions made from cold analysis get overturned from feeling and back again, so the person is effectively working against themselves.

### Urgency Because It Will Go Back Underground
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Why a fearful-avoidant need arrives with a deadline attached. Some part of the system knows the need is normally repressed, so its brief appearance in awareness feels like the only chance it will get. The urgency is not about the partner's response time; it is about the closing window, which is why postponing feels like abandonment of the need rather than management of it.
