### Urgency Is The Nervous System
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her closing principle, and a portable one: if something feels as though it must be settled immediately, that reading is usually coming from a threat response rather than from the problem. Genuine problems generally survive a delay, and the delay is what makes a decent answer possible.

### Wanting The Other Person To Go First
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Fearful-avoidants arrive warm, present and genuinely interested, and are good at making people feel safe to open up — so a conversation can feel deeply connecting and, on reflection, contain almost nothing about them. Priebe notes this makes the style easy to mistake for secure at first meeting: no coldness, no frantic energy, and no disclosure either.

### We Seek What Is Familiar, Not What Is Healthiest
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Attraction tracks recognition rather than benefit. If the dynamic you grew up inside required you to over-assert your needs or over-assert your boundaries, that is the dynamic that will read as love later, and you will keep selecting for it until the underlying adaptation changes. It is the reason anxious and avoidant people find each other so reliably.

### Where The Strategy Still Works
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The areas producing visible chaos are the easy ones — the pain supplies the motivation. The hard ones are where the insecure strategy is currently delivering: the job in a dishonest industry where suspicion of everyone is an asset, the relationship where a persona keeps the peace. Priebe's claim is that these are the areas requiring the most work, and the ones nobody is inclined to touch.

### Where Your Centre Of Gravity Sits
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's somatic map of the three states, learned from having run all of them. Secure: centred in yourself, aware of your own interior and of the people around you at the same time. Deactivated: centred so far inside your own body that everyone has to be pushed out of orbit before you can relax. Activated: centred inside somebody else — the part of you that knows how to make you okay is in them, so they have to be got back on side first.

### White-Knuckling Instead Of Asking Why It Is Hard
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's objection to the standard advice, which she says attachment content actively reinforces. The anxious partner is told to give more space and grits their way through it while their body is on fire; the avoidant partner grits their way toward a commitment they have not examined. Both skip the question worth asking — what would I have to learn for this to feel bearable rather than survived?

### Window Of Tolerance
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The physiological range within which a person can stay present with what they are feeling and still choose how to respond. Above it is fight-or-flight, below it is shutdown; outside it in either direction, choice is not really available.

  - derived_from → Dan Siegel (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=605)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @605s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=605

### You Are Already Vulnerable
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The challenger position starts from the fact that you are affected by every person and situation you engage with, whether or not you concede it. Priebe's line to the avoidant reader is that closing off does not remove the feelings, it only routes them out sideways — so given that you are exposed either way, you may as well pick an exposure that takes you somewhere you want to be.

### You Are Making Me Sick
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant takes the dose, has the reaction, and locates its cause in the person who supplied it — the love must have been wrong, because the need for it is real. Priebe says plainly that of all the styles this one is most likely to be emotionally abusive toward a partner, while insisting on both halves of her standard framing: the wiring was not chosen, and dismantling it is nonetheless the person's own responsibility.

### You Cannot Dance If You Cannot Hear The Music
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's image for what analysis alone cannot do. You can learn every step and still look wrong if you cannot hear the music. She notes how often an avoidant partner in a heated conflict is not looking at the other person at all — eyes off to one side, working out the logic — which is well-intentioned and is half of what repair takes. The other half is being in front of them, feeling alongside them, responding as it happens.

### You Cannot Hold A Boundary You Cannot Live Inside
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's explanation for why anxiously attached people are the most aware they need boundaries and the least able to keep them. A boundary is a space you must then self-regulate inside — and the thing they regulate with is on the other side of it. So the boundary goes up, the dysregulation arrives, and the boundary comes straight back down. It is not weakness of will; it is the design.

### You Cannot Open Someone Else
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her closing note, addressed to the partners rather than the person. Reassurance that you will not reject them does not reach the mechanism, because the rejection is internal. She adds an uncomfortable point: the patterns exist because they worked, and prising them open in someone who has not chosen the work is not obviously a kindness.

*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Priebe quotes Sherry Argov to the effect that people with real power do not explain why they deserve respect — they simply decline to engage with those who withhold it. She offers it as the secure stance: no case is made, because there is no soulmate fantasy requiring this particular person to come round.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The stoicism and self-containment that first appealed is avoidant patterning. The pursuit and the constant validation that felt so good is anxious patterning. Priebe's uncomfortable corollary: asking your partner to become secure is asking them to lose the quality that drew you in — and you may not, on inspection, want the version of them that results.

### Your Inconsistency Is Part Of The Dynamic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Weeks deactivated, then activated in an argument, then unsure whether you want the relationship at all — and no sense of what that does to the person on the other side. Priebe describes assuming it was her partner's job to be vulnerable first and their problem if they were not, before recognising that a partner's chronic dysregulation can be a reasonable response to never knowing which version of you arrives.

### Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility
*origin · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The developmental condition behind avoidant patterning: reaching toward a caregiver in vulnerability or need predictably produced withdrawal or hostility rather than attunement. The lesson learned is not that people are bad, but that expressing need is what costs you them.

  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @850s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=850

### Frightening Caregiver
*origin · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The condition in which the person who supplies everything you need to survive is also the source of danger. Her framing is that this need not be literal lethal threat — a caregiver who periodically loses control of themselves is, to an infant, an enormous animal in the room whose behaviour cannot be predicted, and the child has no coherent answer to whether approaching is safe.

  - mirrors → Inconsistent Responsiveness (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=179)
  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @179s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=179

### Inconsistent Responsiveness
*origin · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Care that arrived sometimes and not others. She is careful that this need not involve anything nameable as neglect — a parent with several children, an illness, exhausting work, or simply their own unprocessed material can produce it while trying hard. What the child registers is not cruelty but unpredictability.

  - mirrors → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=67)
  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @67s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=67

### Intervention Only At Crisis Level
*origin · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Care that arrived reliably but late — around seven to nine out of ten, by which point the child was already outside the window of tolerance. She draws a precise consequence: outside that window nobody absorbs the regulation being performed on them, so the soothing works in the moment and is never learned.

  - mirrors → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=485)
  - part_of → The Distress Scale (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=485)
  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @485s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=485

### Misattuned Mirroring
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A caregiver who cannot tolerate a feeling in themselves reflects back something other than what the child is having — meeting sadness with insistent cheerfulness, well meant and inaccurate. Since children learn what they are feeling from how it is named for them, the result is lasting uncertainty about one's own internal states.

  - source: Learning Self-Regulation Through Self-Attunement @200s — https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=200

### Over-Identification With The Child
*origin · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

One of two failure modes she contrasts with sensitive parenting: the child's state read as a verdict on the parent. The distress then has to be pushed away, because the alternative is accepting the verdict — so the feeling gets managed for the parent's sake rather than the child's.

  - mirrors → Under-Identification With The Child (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=242)

### Sensitive Parenting
*origin · literature · secure=secure-form*

The caregiving that produces security, and she is emphatic it is not perfect caregiving. It is emotional attunement plus the capacity to repair after a rupture — which means securely attaching parents are the ones you hear apologising most, not least.

  - mirrors → Inconsistent Responsiveness (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=121)
  - mirrors → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=121)

### Subtle Discomfort At Negative Emotion
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

No cruelty and no hitting — a parent who was themselves taught to suppress, and who becomes slightly stressed or faintly contemptuous when the child shows something negative. The child reads the difference in warmth precisely and concludes, without any of this reaching words, that cheerfulness is what buys access.

  - mirrors → Misattuned Mirroring (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=300)
  - contrasts_with → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=460)

### The Family Scapegoat Role
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The child who breaks the unspoken rule that the family's dysfunction is not discussed, and is called crazy, irrational or over-reacting for it. Priebe suspects this background sits behind most fearful-avoidant development: a healthy response to injustice gets pathologised until the child concludes that any anger it feels is evidence of its own malfunction.

  - mirrors → Attachment-Seeking Met With Hostility (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=200)
  - source: How The Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Deals With Anger @200s — https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=200

### The Trauma Of What Didn't Happen
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The absence Priebe says gets missed most often — people recognise themselves in the symptoms and can point to nothing in their childhood that was overtly traumatic. What did not happen was being taught to make sense of the relationship between an inner world and an outer one. Research links a subset of depression, anxiety, complex trauma, addiction, insecure attachment and dysregulation back to it.

  - mirrors → Misattuned Mirroring (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=120)
  - contrasts_with → Sensitive Parenting (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=380)

### Under-Identification With The Child
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The other failure mode: practical provision treated as the whole of the job, with warmth and responsiveness not counted as needs at all. Nothing bad has happened, so the child is left to manage the feeling alone — which is precisely the lesson that gets learned.

  - contrasts_with → Separation Between Parent And Child (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=242)
  - source: Early Experiences Of The Secure Attachment Style @242s — https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=242

### Unprocessable Emotion In The Caregiver
*origin · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Why insecure attachment runs in families without anyone intending it. A parent can only teach a child to metabolise the emotions they can metabolise themselves; the ones they cannot get quietly rejected, often by a parent convinced they are being fully available. Her example is a parent whose own shame fires whenever their child gets angry.

  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @188s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=188

### Withheld Information
*origin · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Growing up without access to the information needed to make sense of what is happening. Her worked example is a parent displacing rage about a spouse's affair onto the child who resembles them: the punishment is real and its actual cause is hidden, so neither reasoning nor feeling ever becomes a reliable predictor.

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @1065s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=1065

## practice

### A Boundary With Your Own Triggered Self
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Boundaries you set from a regulated state about a state you will not be in. Priebe's own is leaving the room once anger passes a known threshold — read, run, do anything physiological — rather than trying to solve the problem through the person. She keeps it imperfectly and says imperfectly has still changed her close relationships materially.

  - requires → Setting A Boundary You Control (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=850)
  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=880)
  - contrasts_with → An Apology Must Promise It Will Never Happen Again (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=760)
  - source: What To Do When You Mess Up (Attachment Healing) @850s — https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=850

### Accountability Through Community
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Putting yourself where people who care about you will expect you to make things right. Her diagnosis is structural rather than moral: when relationships sit outside any shared community, disappearing from someone is available at no cost, and shame will generally take that exit over a difficult conversation.

  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=621)
  - requires → Practising Humility (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=621)
  - source: Cultivating The Ability To Tolerate Emotional Discomfort @621s — https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=621

### Acknowledging The Feeling, Not The Logic
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The central move, and she rates it the most useful thing in the video. Grant the feeling fully and hypothetically — if that were what was happening, of course it would hurt, it would hurt me too — then say plainly what is actually the case. Most of what you say is about the emotion; a small part addresses the facts. Disputing the reasoning first is heard as denying that the feeling is real.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=836)
  - requires → Taking Your Partner At Face Value (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=836)
  - contrasts_with → Sequence Analysis (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=481)
  - source: Navigating Conflict With An Anxiously Attached Partner @836s — https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=836

### Admitting You Got It Wrong
*practice · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her clearest picture of why security does not require competence. A guide who admits not knowing and goes to find out beats one who takes the question as an insult; and a guide who comes back to say the directions were wrong beats one who insists they were right and suggests your sense of direction is the problem. The second leaves the child's reading of reality intact; the third damages it.

  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - requires → Naming Hurt And Repairing (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - contrasts_with → Insisting You Were Right (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962)
  - source: Early Experiences Of The Secure Attachment Style @962s — https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=962

### Agreeing Expectations Explicitly
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Say the expectation aloud and get an actual yes. Holding someone to terms they never agreed to is unfair in both directions, and leaves you depending on something you have no way of knowing will arrive.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=90)

### Agreeing When To Return To It
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

End an unfinished conversation by naming when it resumes, then let the ordinary tone come back if that is honest. It answers something specific on the avoidant side — the worry that anything unresolved will resurface sideways — and it gives the other person the time in which their emotional read actually becomes available to them.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=752)
  - requires → Framing It As A Shared Problem (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=752)

  - part_of → Predictability Restores Calm (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=481)

### Apologising With An Action Plan
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Express the remorse, say plainly what you can see it cost them — and then name the wound that is still unhealed, so the other person has enough of the picture to draw their own boundaries. Priebe calls this an adult thing to do rather than a shameful one, and says people can tell when they are being handed the truth, which is why it settles them more than a promise does.

  - requires → Naming It Before Apologising (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=560)
  - requires → Repair Without Needing Forgiveness (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=640)

### Asking For Their Side
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her addition beyond the usual advice about I-statements: having said what it is like for you, ask what it is like for them. Stating your side and then leaving space is the difference between two accounts existing at once and one person's reading being installed as the truth.

  - regulates → Fear Of Engulfment (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=505)
  - requires → Taking Your Partner At Face Value (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=505)

### Asking How Old You Feel
*practice · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Put the question to the distressed part directly: how old do you think I am? Priebe found the answer was rarely a competent woman in her thirties — it was a small child with no means of looking after herself. Naming the number is what makes the gap visible, and the work that follows is bringing your actual age back into the body rather than arguing with the feeling.

  - derived_from → Richard Schwartz (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=350)
  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=400)

  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @350s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=350

### Asking What You Are Actually Arguing For
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

In the middle of a conflict, ask what you are so intent on securing that you would sacrifice either your partner or yourself to get it. Her examples are unflattering by design — preserving their picture of you as good, or keeping decision-making control — and that discomfort is the point, since these are exactly the wants nobody states aloud.

  - regulates → Contempt (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1686)
  - requires → Reading Contempt As A Signal (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1686)

  - part_of → The Loaded Argument (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=529)

### Asking What You Are Expecting, And Whether You Said It
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Treat resentment as a prompt rather than a verdict: what am I expecting here, and have I ever made it explicit? Priebe suggests raising it lightly — admitting you have been waiting to be mind-read, and asking whether they are up for it. She notes what surfaces on the way: fear of rejection, and shame at having wants at all, which is where the healing actually happens.

  - requires → Naming The Premise Out Loud (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=480)
  - regulates → Resentment (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=500)

### Asking What You Would Do If You Were Single
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's own worked case: triggered, on a train home early, texted that her partner could not meet her — and rage. Instead of turning the dial up she asked what she would do if there were no partner at all. A bath, a friend, some writing, a long sleep, a coffee out in the morning. Only once those options were visible could she go back and say honestly what was happening and propose meeting the next day instead.

  - requires → Dispersing Your Needs (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=1000)
  - regulates → Emotional Flashback (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=1020)

  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @1000s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=1000

### Bringing The Feeling Without An Explanation
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Making it safe to say: I feel this, I do not know what it is about, can we look at it together. Priebe frames the payoff as accuracy — a relationship where feelings can arrive un-rationalised is one where problems get worked at the level they exist at, which makes them solvable instead of recurrent.

  - requires → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=960)

### Building The Capacity To Receive
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The work the soup metaphor points at, and it differs by style. The anxious spectrum builds a relationship with itself so that incoming care has somewhere to land rather than being consumed on contact. The avoidant learns to tell safe from unsafe accurately enough to stop treating all of it as suspect. Priebe is direct that this usually needs professional help and takes a long time.

  - requires → Learning To Self-Soothe (https://youtu.be/k4P4Jr8XSVU?t=620)
  - contrasts_with → The Hustle For Worthiness (https://youtu.be/k4P4Jr8XSVU?t=730)
  - source: Attachment Styles And The 'Scarce Love Hypothesis' @620s — https://youtu.be/k4P4Jr8XSVU?t=620

### Caring About Something Else More
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A line Priebe has never been able to attribute and has always liked: the only way to stop caring about something is to care about something else far more. Applied to fixation, it beats trying to think less — fill the time and attention with something you actually love, which incidentally restores the self you would otherwise have nothing to bring.

  - requires → Keeping Your Life Outside The Relationship (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=780)
  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=790)

### Checking What Started The Fight
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

At the end of a conflict, ask what began it and whether it was ever dealt with. Priebe's diagnosis of recurring fights is that the defensive responses generate so many secondary problems — the shutting down, the insults, the days spent on those — that the original issue is lost. An unresolved issue returns, which is why the same fight keeps arriving.

  - requires → Asking What You Are Actually Arguing For (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=1450)
  - mirrors → Agreeing When To Return To It (https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=1470)

  - source: Top 10 Mistakes Anxious/Avoidant Couples Make (And How To Fix Them) @1450s — https://youtu.be/B8128dipzGw?t=1450

### Checking What Your Friends Know
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Compare what your inner circle knows about your doubts, frustrations and private judgements of your partner against what your partner knows. The gap is a direct measure of how much of the relationship is running on undisclosed terms — and if the gap is too insulting to close, that is itself the finding.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443)
  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @1443s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1443
  - mirrors → Venting Instead Of Being Vulnerable (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=1210)

### Checking Whether It Pulls You In Or Out
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The practical test Priebe offers for telling the two apart in the moment. Guilt moves you toward the person — you want to reach out and put it right. Shame moves you away from everyone, including them. If the impulse is to disappear, what is running is shame, and whatever guilt sits under it has not been reached yet.

  - requires → Naming The Feeling Accurately (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=780)
  - part_of → Guilt Versus Shame (https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=480)
  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @780s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=780

### Checking Yourself For Congruence
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Catch the small dishonesties: fine when you are not fine, of course I'm not mad when your body is broadcasting otherwise. Priebe suggests a gradient rather than a switch — ten per cent more congruent, then twenty, then thirty. The reason is mechanical: people cannot attune to what you are hiding, so incongruence is what keeps the feedback you never got as a child from arriving now.

  - requires → Naming The Feeling Accurately (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1330)
  - regulates → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1360)

  - source: Attunement: How Securely Attached People Develop Intimacy @1330s — https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1330

### Congratulating Yourself For Catching It
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The first thing after recognising a bad reaction is usually self-attack, and Priebe argues the opposite is warranted. Acting badly without knowing it is where you were; acting badly and knowing it is a different position, and doing otherwise is only reachable from here. She notes what is being given up in the trade — righteous anger is terrible for the soul and excellent for the ego.

  - requires → Naming The Feeling Accurately (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=250)
  - contrasts_with → Something Is Wrong With Me (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=260)

### Counting The Asymmetry
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Because the imbalance is invisible from inside, count it. For every date they arrange, how many do you? For every night at yours, how many at theirs? How much have you disclosed against how much they have? How often do you go to them for support against how often they come to you? A large gap in any column is the yellow flag.

  - requires → Tracking What You Receive (https://youtu.be/TOGI3Zi7aX8?t=500)
  - contrasts_with → The Proximity-Seeking Blindspot (https://youtu.be/TOGI3Zi7aX8?t=480)
  - source: Avoidant Attachment: Check These 5 Blindspots If Your Relationship Is Stuck In Conflict Cycles @500s — https://youtu.be/TOGI3Zi7aX8?t=500

### Dating Yourself
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Take the effort you would put into courting someone and put it into yourself: turn up on time, keep the commitments, know your own wants well enough to meet them, buy the small gifts, speak kindly. Priebe is explicit that mantras will not do it — it is the same slow work of getting to know someone, run on yourself, over a long period.

  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=620)
  - regulates → Never Good Enough (https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=590)

### Deciding Not To Decide
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Recognise the activated state and rule yourself out of decisions while you are in it, on the reasoning that a genuinely important decision can survive a delay. The premise underneath is that there is a calmer version of you that ought to be the one deciding, and it is not currently available.

  - regulates → Approach-Avoidance Conflict (https://youtu.be/ZvqnHlHlqzM?t=124)

### Designing A Life Without The Partner
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her exercise, and a demanding one: plan your life on the certainty that the relationship is never coming. What you would do with your time, which friendships and family you would invest in, what you would build, what you would take up with the hours currently spent tracking someone else. The point is not resignation — it is that boundaries need something to enclose. Her image is being handed fencing materials without knowing where your land ends.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=728)
  - requires → Dispersing Your Needs (https://youtu.be/VBJyaBy_kxQ?t=728)

### Dispersing Your Needs
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

She is pointed that anxiously attached people do not have more needs than anyone else — they route too many of them through a single relationship. The work is not having fewer needs but spreading them across self-regulation, a partner and a wider community, so no one connection is carrying all of it.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=845)
  - requires → Intervening At Low Distress (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=845)

### Doing Something A Child Could Not Do
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Write the list while calm: things a seven-year-old could not possibly do. Then when the flashback arrives, do one. Priebe's are deliberately mundane — clear the accounting, sort the tax, cook a proper adult meal, buy your own clothes, ring someone about a project without mentioning the conflict. The point is not distraction; it is physical evidence handed to a part of you that has the wrong number.

  - requires → Asking How Old You Feel (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=1220)
  - regulates → Emotional Flashback (https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=1240)

### Dropping Attachment To Outcome
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A conversation entered with a hope — that they like you, that they say a particular thing, that it lands somewhere specific — is a conversation being steered rather than had. Priebe's instruction is to notice the script running, let it run without following it, and get authentically curious about what the other person is actually saying. You learn far more, far faster.

  - part_of → Presence And Curiosity Versus Strategy And Analysis (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1600)

### Dropping The Defences
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her own account, and the most concrete instruction in the video. Noticing the defences coming up as raised fists — the internal cataloguing of everything the other person has wrong — and deliberately letting them drop, so the words arrive. She describes coming away feeling beaten up, still convinced the accusations were untrue, and clear for the first time that being spoken to that way by someone she loved hurt regardless of its accuracy.

  - regulates → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=845)
  - requires → Re-Sensitizing To Your Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/esJj49ARgVA?t=845)

### Earning Your Own Trust By Following Through
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Telling the activated part that it has real information, that now is the wrong moment, and that this will be handled tomorrow — then handling it. Priebe is blunt about the second half: if you do not follow through, you will not believe yourself the next time, and the urgency will be correct. She describes her own version, having the hard conversations the next day, and the triggers losing their emergency quality as a result.

  - requires → Making An Appointment With The Feeling (https://youtu.be/QrhIWeLBkDQ?t=590)

### Expressing Anger At Two Out Of Ten
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Deliberately raising things while they are still minor, on the reasoning that smallness is the reason to speak rather than the reason to stay quiet. It requires overriding the standing veto every time, and it feels absurd — Priebe says the frustration of doing it is real, and that it is nonetheless the route to anger arriving in the situations that actually produced it.

### Finding A Container For Each Emotion
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe lists her own, and the specificity is the point: a somatic therapist and the radical honesty community for anger, authentic relating for intimacy, Tantra for sexuality, Buddhism for grief and staying present with pain. Cognitive understanding is not what changes these — being in the feeling with someone trained to hold it is. She describes anger reliably producing a pain flare or an urge to drink until that changed.

  - derived_from → Radical Honesty (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=1990)

### Finding An Earned-Secure Model
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her practical suggestion for starting the avoidant version of this work: find someone who arrived at security by working for it, rather than someone who never had to. She notes a specific cascade — avoidant people tend to respect one another, so watching someone they respect do the work without becoming a mess can reclassify it from pathetic to worth doing.

  - regulates → Self-Disgust At Your Own Need (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=985)
  - requires → Sensitizing, Then Sharing (https://youtu.be/c-_5VH-aXdM?t=985)

### Finding The Paramedics Elsewhere
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Relational wounds do need laying out — but not to someone who is having a hard time of their own in the same conversation. Priebe's move is to go somewhere else for the regulation first: another person, time alone, therapy. Then return to the conflict able to say what the issue actually was, rather than doing whatever it takes to be liked again.

  - requires → Learning To Self-Soothe (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=620)
  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=600)

### Flagging That This One Is Tender
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Say in advance that what you are about to do is difficult for you and that you may be unsteady around it. Priebe pairs this with the harder half — coaching yourself that a sensitive area does not oblige your partner to respond perfectly; they are also entitled to their own reaction. She describes having to go back days later to say plainly that something needed more attention than it got.

  - requires → Naming Your Own Activation Out Loud (https://youtu.be/09SXYct7LDQ?t=1330)
  - regulates → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/09SXYct7LDQ?t=1450)

### Framing It As A Shared Problem
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Bring the issue as something costing you both — time, energy, repeated arguments — and ask to work out an approach together, rather than leading with how it made you feel. Not because the feeling is irrelevant, but because a request to collaborate on a shared difficulty does not trip the engulfment alarm the way a request to change does.

  - regulates → Fear Of Engulfment (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=177)
  - requires → Naming The Feeling Accurately (https://youtu.be/oOOx0rj8Qas?t=177)

### Going Where Vulnerability Is The Norm
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A trick that works with fearful-avoidant patterning rather than against it: the guard drops most easily where someone else was vulnerable first. So change the environment before expecting to change yourself — rooms with explicit rules about sharing and containment, and people who are emotionally fluent. Priebe notes those people feel threatening precisely because you expect them to see through you, and that they are the ones most likely to help.

  - requires → Accountability Through Community (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=830)
  - contrasts_with → The Social Mask (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=900)

### Holding The Hurt Child's Hand
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

When a partner's mood registers as rejection, Priebe pictures the hurt part of herself as a child, takes its hand, and tells it plainly that this is the other person having a hard day and that nothing is wrong with it — then goes and does something else, returning to the relationship for repair once both people are in a better state. It works because the instinct to protect a child is one most people already have.

  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=1000)
  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/7DenwDgrrbU?t=1030)

### Holding Two Things At Once
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Keeping the explanation and the impact in view together rather than letting one dissolve the other. For some people this is where recognising actual neglect or abuse becomes possible for the first time — not because the account of why changes, but because it stops being a reason the harm did not count.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=171)

### Intervening At Low Distress
*practice · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Treat your own distress as worth acting on around three to six out of ten, while options are still available. Her analogy is shopping for food before you are hungry: at a moderate level you can try a conversation, a limit, a change of approach and see how each lands; at eight or nine you are no longer choosing between options, only seeking relief.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=485)

### Inviting The Direct Statement
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Saying, in advance and without heat, that the story is not what you need — that you would rather be told the feeling and the need directly, and that you will take them seriously when you are. Priebe is careful that this is not indulging the strategy: it removes the reason for the strategy by making the direct route the one that works.

  - requires → Validating The Feeling Without Justifying It (https://youtu.be/GE0iRhskMW8?t=505)

### Keeping Both Faculties Online
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Holding the emotional self available while reasoning and the reasoning self available while feeling. She frames this as the specific advantage of the fearful-avoidant position: both capacities are already there and consciously accessible, just never at the same moment, so the work is closing that gap rather than building something absent.

  - regulates → Approach-Avoidance Conflict (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=1452)

### Keeping Your Life Outside The Relationship
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Her prescription for the lean-anxious version, and a preventative one. If the pattern is to go fully into a relationship and later recoil at everything you gave up, the work is refusing to make those changes in the first place — naming specific commitments that remain yours and keeping them, especially while you most want to abandon them.

  - regulates → Approach-Avoidance Conflict (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1332)

### Learning To Self-Soothe
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Building the missing half of regulation: staying with a strong feeling and bringing yourself down from it without requiring someone else to do the work. She is direct that this usually needs specific therapeutic help rather than resolve.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=966)

### Letting The Nervous System Lead
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Give your body's signals authority roughly half the time, even when they make no case for themselves. She frames it as the same equality a secure relationship needs between two people, applied between a person and their own physiology — a system that never gets to lead is one you are permanently overruling.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=1571)

### Logging State Against Activity
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Check in repeatedly over time, recording what you feel alongside what you were doing, until the pairings become visible. The payoff she describes is deflating in a useful way: what lifts a low mood usually turns out to be sleep, daylight and a conversation rather than anything commensurate with how complicated the feeling seemed.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=523)

### Making An Appointment With The Feeling
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Acknowledge the feeling, park it deliberately, do what you committed to, and set a real time to return to it. It answers both fears at once — the avoidant one that feeling anything means never functioning again, and the anxious one that setting a feeling aside for an hour means everything falls apart.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=662)
  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=662)

### Mapping The Steps To The Future
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Instead of the picture, the route: name the problems in the way, name what would have to change starting now, and raise both with the partner. What you are testing is not whether they agree to the destination but whether they will work the steps. Priebe is clear a secure relationship does not need the ending settled in advance — it needs both people clear about which step they are on.

  - requires → Agreeing Expectations Explicitly (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=1150)

### Mapping Where The Strategy Works
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Going through the areas of your life — relationship, work, family — and naming where the insecure strategy is currently succeeding, with no obligation to change any of it yet. Priebe frames it as putting an asterisk beside those situations and as honouring what the strategy did for your survival, on the grounds that you cannot dismantle something you have not yet seen working.

  - requires → Logging State Against Activity (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=1030)

### Mirroring Back
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Repeat back what you are hearing without endorsing it, and keep asking what else. Agreement is not required — visible calm and attention are. Done enough times it works down from the presenting accusation to the fear underneath it, which is the thing actually worth addressing.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=965)

### Mourning On Purpose
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Six months with no return to the ex and no replacement — a new relationship over an open wound is a dressing that stops it closing. Let the birthday arrive, and the album, and the morning nobody brings coffee, and feel each one pass. Priebe keeps a document of everything she would say to a former partner, thanks and anger both, and still adds to it, which processes the feeling without disturbing their peace.

  - requires → Tolerating Emotional Discomfort (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=930)

### Naming Hurt And Repairing
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Getting to the pain, saying it, and giving the other person a chance to respond. They may respond badly — but writing them off in advance guarantees the repair never becomes available, and keeps you from holding them as someone competent.

  - regulates → Unregistered Hurt (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1092)

### Naming It Before Apologising
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Ask for the hour or the day you actually need, then write down everything that happened with nothing filtered, softened or left out, and read it as data rather than as a charge sheet. Only then decide what resource the situation calls for. Until it can be named accurately there is nothing to change, and nothing honest to promise.

  - requires → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=380)

### Naming The Conflict And Your Intent
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Open by saying plainly that this is a conversation about a problem, that you want to resolve it, and that you are not leaving. Anxious patterning reads the beginning of a conflict as the possible end of the relationship, so removing that ambiguity at the outset changes what the whole exchange is about.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=161)
  - requires → Framing It As A Shared Problem (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=241)

### Naming The Feeling Accurately
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Say what is actually there rather than a verdict about it. Her contrast is calling yourself pathetic when what you are is sad — the first word implies you manufactured the feeling, and a feeling you have accused yourself of inventing cannot be worked with.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=626)

*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Bringing the actual premise into the open where it can be negotiated or refused. She is honest about the risk: a partner may have been drawn to precisely what you were suppressing, and stating your real terms can end things. But until they are stated there is no way to find out which situation you are in.

*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The use of the framework she endorses in conflict: describing your own activation and what it looks like from outside, noting how it may be landing on the other person, and then asking rather than concluding. What makes it legitimate is the direction — it is an account of yourself offered for correction, not a reading of them delivered as fact.

### No Failure, Just Feedback
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The stance Priebe recommends for the long middle of the process: when a new strategy does not hold and the old response wins, the outcome is information about the conditions, not a verdict on the attempt. She is explicit that you will get it wrong repeatedly and that this is what the stage consists of.

*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

When you set a limit, ask what need drove the behaviour and offer a workable route to it. Her own version pairs a refusal to interpret subtext with a standing promise to take any direct concern seriously — the fence has a door, and people are told where it is.

### Owning The Feeling As Yours
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Recognising that a feeling arose in you rather than being placed there by someone else — nobody can transmit an emotion into another person's mind. Doing this consistently corrects the model of what others think, which is what makes the difference between adjusting the wrong things forever and seeing the actual pattern.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1326)

*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Recognising that the pattern of people you go after is a choice you keep making rather than a run of luck. She connects it to what the pursuit is actually looking for — someone whose flat affect reads as capacity — and to the conclusion that the problem is not solved by that person opening up.

### Practising Humility
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Entering a disagreement genuinely open to being the one who is missing something. She ties this to what deep relationships are for — being lovingly challenged and seeing through someone else's eyes — and notes the harder half: accepting that you sometimes hurt people even while deciding as well as you could.

  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=430)

*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Say beforehand what tends to happen to you in conflict and what you will need if it does — a pause, a restatement of what you are both aiming at. She counters a common worry directly: admitting you have feelings does not repel an avoidant partner, because they already know. What overwhelms is strong emotion arriving with no shape to it, and a stated plan gives it shape.

### Re-Contextualizing Your History
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Working back through your own history to find where what you felt genuinely was caused by something outside you, recovering the response a child with full emotional access would have had, and extending that child some compassion from where you stand now.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=961)

### Re-Parenting Yourself
*practice · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Treating yourself the way a well-attuned adult would treat a child in your state: neither dismissing the feeling nor letting it run the day. The two halves are rarely present together — avoidant patterning tends to have the practical half without the attunement, anxious patterning the attunement without the practical half.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=662)

The core of avoidant healing as she frames it: rebuilding access to the feelings that were sorted out of awareness early, rather than acquiring new coping skills on top of the numbness.

*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=feared fearful-avoidant=alternating*

*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Treat the emotions you find most repellent in other people as an index of which emotions were rejected in you. The intensity is the signal, and those are the specific feelings re-sensitization has to start with.

### Reading Your Fantasies For The Need
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Ask not what happens in the fantasy but what you feel in it. Priebe works her own — singing a sad song to a crowd who sing it back, despite not being able to sing — and lands on emotional mirroring: something painful wants to be seen and reflected so she feels less alone. The move is then to find which relationship that need belongs in and ask for it there, rather than leaving it to be met in imagination.

### Reading Your Four-F Responses Backwards
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Not in the moment — afterwards. Look back at the times you froze and withdrew, or went furious, or went scattered and absent, or went into caretaking, and ask what relational need was live underneath. Priebe presents these responses as the body working hard to keep the need out of your awareness, which makes them the most reliable index of what is there.

### Reading Your Relationship History
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Look for what your past partners had in common and compare it with what you say you want. Where the two disagree, the history is the more accurate account, and the difference between them marks the blind spot.

  - regulates → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=2116)

### Repair Without Needing Forgiveness
*practice · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Going to someone you hurt, naming what you did, and staying steady whether or not they accept it. She locates the difficulty precisely: from a shame-based position an honest admission feels like confirming that you are bad, so the apology has to buy something back. Separate the act from the identity and it no longer needs to.

  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=364)
  - requires → Practising Humility (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=364)

### Reviewing The Relationship Objectively
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The counterpart practice: deliberately looking at the relationship from outside the fantasy — journalling, inviting feedback from friends less invested than you, keeping a running practical account of what you are looking for and whether this matches. She notes deactivation is harder to catch than activation because it pulls attention out of the body rather than into it.

  - regulates → Longing At A Safe Distance (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1211)

### Searching For A Nourishing Environment
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A mentor's line Priebe says changed her life: you are used to thinking of your environment as emotionally impoverished, so you stopped looking for evidence otherwise — and healing requires believing there are ways it could nourish you, then going out to find them. The cruelty of the wound is that the thing needed to heal it, mentorship from the environment, is exactly what it tells you is unavailable.

  - requires → Accountability Through Community (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=2180)

### Sensitizing, Then Sharing
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Her prescription for the lean-avoidant version: a daily practice of dropping attention out of the head and into the body to find what is actually there, then saying it somewhere designed to be safe — therapy, a support group, or a friend with whom the commitment is mutual. She is realistic that going from never sharing to sharing openly is too large a step to take at once.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1090)

### Setting A Boundary You Control
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Phrase the limit as your own action and nothing else: what you will do if a thing happens. Her worked correction is instructive — wanting a partner not to insult you is a fair expectation, and the boundary that belongs beside it is ending the conversation when they do.

  - regulates → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=413)

### Setting Boundaries With Yourself First
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe is blunt that the fix is not better boundaries with other people. It is learning what a boundary violation feels like in your body, acquiring the self-soothing to sit inside the boundary once it is set, and committing to yourself that you will leave situations where you are treated badly. Self-soothing is hard here because being alone with yourself brings the self-hatred up, which is where inner-child work comes in.

  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=520)

### Starting With A Paid Witness
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's own sequence, over years: for the first year, one intimate relationship and nothing else; then a therapist, where being honest could be practised with someone trained to receive it; then, after about a year of that, one deeply honest friendship; then the skill generalised to new friends and communities. The order matters — the first step is with someone whose job is to not flinch.

  - requires → Sensitizing, Then Sharing (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=660)

### Taking The Challenger Position
*practice · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Instead of specifying what the other person must change, ask what you could learn or build if nothing around you changes at all. It invites you rather than your environment to be the thing that moves.

  - part_of → The Empowerment Dynamic (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=555)

### Taking The Coach Position
*practice · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Treat other people as capable of acting on their own behalf, and remind them of it when they have forgotten — rather than becoming the reason they manage. She is careful that this does not assume equal circumstances, only equal capacity to act within them.

  - part_of → The Empowerment Dynamic (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=555)

### Taking The Creator Position
*practice · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Ask what is still available to you, granting the whole grievance. Her own account of learning this is a counsellor who declined to discuss what her partner was doing wrong and asked instead what was keeping her there — a question that turned an inventory of someone else's failings into a list of things she could actually do.

  - part_of → The Empowerment Dynamic (https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=555)

### Taking Turns As The Secure Base
*practice · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Nobody is regulated all the time, so both people need to be able to absorb the other's bad day — and to do it according to what that person actually needs rather than what they themselves would want. Some need space, some need company. The requirement is that it goes both ways and that it flexes.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=601)
  - requires → Taking Your Partner At Face Value (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=601)

### Taking Your Partner At Face Value
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Presenting your own position without editing and receiving theirs without decoding it. She draws a hard line here: if the only way you can get your needs met is by obscuring, exaggerating or managing your partner, the secure move is not better technique but not being that close to that person — and the same holds if you feel you must handle them as too fragile or unequal to hear the truth.

  - regulates → Contempt (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1982)
  - requires → Naming The Premise Out Loud (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=1982)

  - manifests_as → Naming The Fantasy (https://youtu.be/-rQR-XduvU0?t=321)

### Telling People You Are Practising
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Telling safe people in advance that you are learning to raise small things, and that if something sounds trivial it is because you are trying to catch it early rather than because it is secretly enormous. Priebe adds the in-the-moment version too — saying outright that this is a two out of ten and feels silly to mention. Both remove the need for the thing to be big enough to justify itself.

  - requires → Naming Your Own Activation Out Loud (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=670)

### Telling The Protective Part You Have Another Way
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Being present feels threatening because a part of you is insisting that the strategy is what keeps you from being abandoned, and that this present-moment business has nothing to offer. Priebe's move is to sit with that part rather than override it — to say that there is now another way of getting the same needs met, and that it is not being abandoned in the process.

  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=1900)

### Testing The Rule Before Leaving
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Before ending a relationship that has gone empty, name the rule you have been obeying and find out whether it is real. Priebe describes doing exactly this — laying out her aversion to setting boundaries in her own space, and her fear that doing so made her a bad person — and finding her partner carrying an equivalent set of invisible rules. She came out of it more attracted to him than before.

  - requires → Naming The Premise Out Loud (https://youtu.be/09SXYct7LDQ?t=480)

### The Four-Year-Old Test
*practice · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's question before re-entering a relationship: if you were responsible for a four-year-old, would you let her live with this person — and if so, what would have to be in place to keep her safe through the fights and the unavailable stretches? A clear no means the inner parenting to survive that dynamic is not there yet, whatever you decide about the person.

  - requires → Re-Parenting Yourself (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=460)
  - mirrors → Holding The Hurt Child's Hand (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=480)

  - source: Anxious Attachment: 5 Questions To Ask Yourself Before Getting Back Together With An Ex @460s — https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=460

### The No-Contact Test
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Do not end a relationship unless you are prepared to cut contact completely — Priebe suggests six months as the benchmark. Willingness to do that is the test: if you cannot, what you are feeling is overwhelm rather than a decision, and the work is inside the relationship. She is direct that staying friends without firm internal boundaries is unfair to the other person and to yourself.

  - requires → Reviewing The Relationship Objectively (https://youtu.be/-PCcJsp30AA?t=790)

### Tolerating Emotional Discomfort
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

She names this as the single capacity that most determines whether someone can sustain close relationships. What distinguishes secure relating is not an absence of conflict but staying calm, regulated and present inside it — able to be vulnerable without requiring the other person to fix how you feel, and to hear something ego-threatening without defending.

  - regulates → Emotional Dysregulation (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=70)

### Tracking What You Receive
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Deliberately keeping in view what the relationship gives you, not only what it asks of you. Without that side of the ledger the trade-off is unreadable, and the resentment that follows is arithmetic rather than character.

  - regulates → Loss Of Attraction (https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1212)

### Treating Emotion As Data
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Take what you feel as a data point worth entering into the decision rather than a verdict to obey or a fault to correct. Not following every impulse and not discarding logic — simply having more information than before. She points out the cost of leaving it out: plans made without the emotional cost accounted for are where a lot of burnout comes from.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/ssB6tsIxlls?t=105)

### Un-gaslighting Yourself
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Before treating a feeling as distortion, asking what it is accurately observing. Priebe's objection to the standard reassurance is that being told a fear is all in your head, when the fear is measuring a real barrier, teaches you to stop trusting your own instrument. The move is to separate the part that is a real read from the part that is an old wound colouring a new situation — and to keep both.

  - requires → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/k4P4Jr8XSVU?t=210)

### Validating The Feeling Without Justifying It
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Letting a feeling be real without first proving the external circumstances warrant it, and separating what you feel from what you must therefore do. Most insecure patterning fuses the two, so that admitting jealousy seems to commit you to acting on it.

  - regulates → Desensitization To One's Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=476)
  - requires → Re-Sensitizing To Your Own Emotions (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=476)

### Watching Yourself With The Sound Off
*practice · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

With the other person's consent, record a conflict and watch it back muted — or sit in front of a mirror during one, which is clumsier but works. The question is what emotion the body language alone conveys, and how someone sensitive to contempt would receive it. Priebe offers it as the most direct route to information you cannot get from inside your own head.

  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @600s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=600

### Lundy Bancroft
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Runs anger-management programmes and wrote Why Does He Do That? Priebe quotes his line to people entering those programmes — that the problem is not an anger problem but an abuse problem — as the cleanest statement of the difference between having a feeling and what you gave yourself permission to do with it.

  - source: Fearful-Avoidant TRIGGERS: Managing The Shame Of Having Needs And The Guilt Of Taking Space @830s — https://youtu.be/QrhIWeLBkDQ?t=830

### Martin M. Broadwell
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Credited with the first description of the four-stage learning model in 1969, later restated by Curtis and Warren and popularised by Noel Burch at Gordon Training International as the four stages of learning any new skill. Priebe traces the attribution herself and notes the model was never intended for psychotherapy — she applies it because attachment healing is a learning process.

  - source: The 4 Stages Of Attachment Healing (Conscious Competency Model) @30s — https://youtu.be/GbWAlMQkWzo?t=30

### Mary Ainsworth
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Developed the Strange Situation, the procedure by which infant attachment was first categorised — and the source of the original lettered clusters that later acquired the names avoidant, secure and anxious.

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @58s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=58

### Nonviolent Communication
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The system Priebe recommends specifically to avoidant-spectrum people learning to state a boundary: it works by going underneath irritation or overwhelm to the unmet need beneath, and by phrasing it so the other person can actually respond. Her argument is pragmatic — telling someone their feelings are unwarranted, even where true, does not produce the outcome you wanted.

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @900s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=900

### Patricia Crittenden
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Worked under Ainsworth and developed the Dynamic Maturation Model, which treats the avoidant and anxious categories as gradients with sub-scales rather than boxes.

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @581s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=581

### Patricia DeYoung
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Author of Understanding and Treating Chronic Shame, which Priebe cites for its definition of shame as the sense of one's self disintegrating in the presence of a dysregulating other — the formulation that explains why shame and attachment fuse so early and so tightly.

  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @300s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=300

### Radical Honesty
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The practice Priebe credits with changing how she handles anger: expressing it clearly and cleanly at the moment it is felt, rather than carrying it in the body as resentment until it comes out all at once.

  - source: How The Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Deals With Anger @790s — https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=790

### Richard Schwartz
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Developed Internal Family Systems; Priebe calls No Bad Parts a brilliant introduction to it. The question she takes from him and uses constantly — ask the distressed part how old it thinks you are — is the hinge of this whole video.

  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @340s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=340

### Ross Ellenhorn
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Author of How We Change (and Ten Reasons Why We Don't), which Priebe names as one of her favourite books. Its subject is the one she reaches at the end of this video: why behaviour we consciously want gone persists, because unconsciously it is paying for itself.

  - source: What To Do When You Mess Up (Attachment Healing) @1050s — https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=1050

### Scattered Minds
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Gabor Maté's book on inattentive thinking and its links to a disorganised attachment system, which Priebe cites when discussing why fearful-avoidants so often reach for stimulation and large ambitions rather than sitting with pain.

  - source: 10 Signs You May Have A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style @3180s — https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=3180

### Stephen Karpman
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Devised the drama triangle in the late 1960s, out of transactional analysis — the study of how unresolved childhood material gets projected onto present relationships.

  - source: Attachment Styles & The Drama Triangle (Part 1): Intro To The Drama Triangle @1s — https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=1

### Thais Gibson
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Runs the Personal Development School, where Priebe took courses. Priebe credits her as the first person she heard describe the avoidant spectrum as people with rich inner lives rather than as antagonists, and the deactivating-strategy vocabulary used across this corpus comes from that work.

  - source: What Are The 4 Attachment Styles? @1660s — https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=1660

### The Betrayal Bond
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A book Priebe cites not for its attachment content — she does not recall it addressing attachment directly — but as an illustration of how thoroughly a person can be adapted to exploitative environments, and of how reliably that adaptation delivers them into more of them.

  - source: Are Fearful-Avoidants Doomed To Have Dysfunctional Relationships? @752s — https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=752

## state

### Accurate Reappraisal
*state · synthesis · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Genuinely concluding, on evidence, that someone is not a good fit. It exists and it matters — which is exactly why deactivation is so convincing, since it arrives wearing the same clothes.

  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @123s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=123

### Approach-Avoidance Conflict
*state · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Both attachment responses live at once, so the system moves toward closeness and away from it in the same moment. She is careful that this runs below conscious intent: the mind may want the relationship while the nervous system refuses to stand down.

  - triggers → Deactivating Strategies (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=300)
  - triggers → Preemptive Sabotage (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=382)
  - originates_in → Frightening Caregiver (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=300)
